findings.title: Presence function disables TLS verification to Postgres
findings.description: The Vercel presence function connects to `CHAT_DATABASE_URL` with `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`, accepting any certificate. A MITM between Vercel and the database can read/alter traffic (including the DB credentials in the connection handshake). The same function caches raw bearer tokens as Map keys for 5 minutes (`idCache`), so a compromised instance holds live tokens.
findings.fix: Use `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: process.env.PG_CA }` (or `sslmode=verify-full` in the URL); key the cache on a SHA-256 of the token rather than the token itself.

findings.title: Vercel chat/presence functions connect to Neon with rejectUnauthorized:false
findings.description: Both serverless functions disable TLS certificate verification to Neon. Neon supports verified TLS (sslmode=verify-full with its CA), so this is an unnecessary downgrade that allows a MITM between Vercel and Neon to read or alter chat/presence data. Same pattern at api/presence.ts:289.
findings.evidence: pool = new pg.Pool({ connectionString: url, max: 2, ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false } });
findings.fix: Use `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true }` with the Neon CA (or `?sslmode=verify-full` in CHAT_DATABASE_URL).

findings.title: Token-storage defence relies on a CSP the page never receives
findings.description: The storage policy says the real mitigation for XSS token theft is "the gateway's CSP (`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'`)" and `.env.production:50-53` repeats that it "applies to the page". The page is served by Vercel (vercel.json), not the gateway; only `/gw/*` is proxied, and vercel.json defines no `headers`, so no CSP, HSTS or frame-ancestors header is delivered with index.html. Tokens therefore sit in sessionStorage with none of the script-injection protection the design assumes; third-party scripts (Privy SDK, model-viewer, any CDN) run unconstrained.
findings.fix: Add a `headers` block to vercel.json with a real CSP (allowing Privy/RPC origins explicitly), `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Content-Type-Options` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`; correct the comments in session.ts and .env.production.

findings.title: boardgame.io Postgres store disables TLS verification even when PGSSL=require
findings.description: The shared pool maps PGSSL=require to rejectUnauthorized:true, but the bgio-postgres/Sequelize store maps every non-'disable' value to rejectUnauthorized:false. The two connections to the same database therefore have different TLS guarantees, and the one carrying all live match state (and the gameover the result recorder trusts) is the weaker one.
findings.evidence:
dialectOptions:
  config.PGSSL !== 'disable' ? { ssl: { require: true, rejectUnauthorized: false } } : {},
findings.fix: Mirror sslConfig(): `require` -> `{ require: true, rejectUnauthorized: true }`, `no-verify` -> `rejectUnauthorized: false`.

findings.title: 'nonce too low' on broadcast is treated as 'already known' success
findings.description: The regex folds 'nonce too low' into the duplicate-broadcast success path. That error also occurs when a *different* transaction consumed the nonce (a manual tx from the escrow key, or a reverted replacement that was mined), in which case this leg's hash will never be found and runLeg returns 'pending' forever (see server-34) instead of surfacing that the nonce was lost.
findings.fix: On 'nonce too low', check getTransactionStatus(prepared.hash); if not found, mark the leg for rebuild with a fresh nonce and alert, rather than returning success.

findings.title: whoCache keeps a bearer token authoritative for 5 min after logout/expiry
findings.description: Identity resolved from /api/profiles/me is cached for 5 minutes keyed on the raw Authorization header. Access tokens are 15-minute JWTs and /auth/logout revokes the session family, but a cached token keeps posting chat as that profile until the cache entry expires. The cache is bounded (clear at 2000) but the clear is a thundering-herd reset rather than LRU, and raw bearer tokens are retained in process memory.
findings.fix: Cap the cache TTL at min(5 min, token exp from the JWT payload) and key on a SHA-256 of the token; consider verifying the JWT locally with JWT_SECRET instead of calling the gateway.

findings.title: Chat admin is granted by a mutable display name, not a profile id
findings.description: NAME_ADMINS matches the gateway's displayName case-insensitively. Display names are user-editable via PATCH /api/profiles/me on the profile service; they are unique, but if the real admin ever renames (or the account is deleted), any player can claim 'anoversizedmoosewithsocks' and gain announce rights in the global hub. Admin should be keyed on the immutable profile id or wallet address (CHAT_ADMINS already supports addresses).
findings.fix: Replace NAME_ADMINS with the admin's profile id (who.id) or move them into CHAT_ADMINS by address.

findings.title: A payout leg that is never mined has no fee-bump path and blocks void
findings.description: If a signed transfer is underpriced or dropped from the mempool, awaitOutcome keeps returning 'pending', the runner rebroadcasts the identical bytes forever, and all later legs (and the escrow) stay pending. repurposePayoutForVoid refuses whenever any leg has a tx_hash, so an operator cannot void either. Funds are effectively frozen until someone edits the database.
findings.fix: After N attempts or T minutes pending, re-sign the leg at the SAME nonce with bumped fees (replace-by-fee), recording the new hash before broadcast; the nonce guarantees mutual exclusion with the old attempt.

findings.title: The rules engine, bot, wager, custodial and Vercel API modules have no tests
findings.description: Front-end tests exist only for cards, collection, error-text, linked-wallets, masterquest lore, match-mode, privy auth-flow/env and ranked-client. The modules that decide game outcomes and move money have none: src/Game.ts (932 lines, all boardgame.io moves and combat), src/bot.ts (389), src/wager-program.ts (400), src/server-custodial.ts (464, custodial escrow settlement), src/booster-mint.ts (319), src/pack-evm.ts (201), api/chat.ts and api/presence.ts (Postgres-backed Vercel functions). Regressions in combat or settlement can only be caught by hand-play.

findings.title: Two backends coexist: insecure legacy server is still `npm start` + render.yaml target
findings.description: Live probe confirms https://api.ocva.online is the new-backend nginx gateway (/healthz -> {service:'gateway'}, /games/ranked/season -> 200) and src/api/config.ts points the client there, so new-backend is the production backend. Yet the repo root's `npm start` still runs src/server.ts, render.yaml still deploys it with CUSTODIAL_ESCROW_KEYPAIR, and tsconfig.json excludes server.ts/db.ts from typechecking. Anyone following the root scripts or the Render blueprint stands up the server with findings server-01..20 and a funded hot wallet. The two servers also duplicate the game rules, deck validation, ranked Glicko-2 and queue logic (src/ranked/* vs new-backend/services/game/src/ranked/*), which will drift.
findings.evidence:
package.json:  "start": "tsx src/server.ts",
render.yaml:  buildCommand: npm ci && npm run build
              startCommand: npm start
              - key: CUSTODIAL_ESCROW_KEYPAIR
tsconfig.json: "exclude": ["src/server.ts", "src/db.ts"]
new-backend/README.md: This replaces the single Koa server in `src/server.ts`.
findings.fix: Delete src/server.ts, src/db.ts, src/server-custodial.ts, src/server-wager.ts, src/ranked/* and render.yaml (or move them to an archive branch), point `npm start` at nothing server-side, and make new-backend the only place game/ranked logic lives (the front end can import the shared cards module).

findings.title: Deposits on a match that never finishes are stuck until an operator voids
findings.description: An escrow can be created on an 'open' match and funded by seat 0 before anyone joins. If the host cancels (POST /games/:id/cancel sets status 'void'), the opponent never joins, or the match is abandoned, no game.match_results row is ever written, and listSettlementCandidates only joins through match_results, so the deposit is never refunded automatically. The only exit is the operator-only /wager/escrows/:id/void, which requires someone to notice.
findings.fix: Add a second worker query that refunds escrows whose game.matches.status is 'void' (or whose match has been 'open' past a TTL) using planVoidRefund, and/or only allow escrow creation once the match is 'live'.

findings.title: Access tokens cannot be revoked before expiry; jti is never checked
findings.description: verifyAccessToken validates signature, iss/aud and exp only. /auth/logout revokes the refresh family, but the 15-minute access token (jti = session id) keeps working on every service until exp, including wager deposit and lobby routes. A stolen access token therefore survives logout; ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SEC may be set as high as 3600.
findings.fix: On logout, write `auth:revoked:<jti>` to Redis with TTL = remaining token life and have requireAuth reject tokens whose jti is present; keep ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SEC short.

findings.title: Deposit verification rejects smart-account wallets the auth service deliberately admits
findings.description: The auth service added ERC-1271/6492 login so 4337 smart accounts can sign in, but verifyDepositTx requires `tx.from` (the EOA that signed the transaction) to be one of the profile's linked addresses. A smart-account deposit is submitted by a bundler/relayer, so tx.from is the bundler and the deposit is rejected with not_sent_by_depositor even though the ERC-20 Transfer log's `from` is the player's account. Those players can log in and open an escrow but never fund it; their tokens sit in the escrow wallet with no deposit row.
findings.fix: Drop the tx.from check (the per-transfer `transfer.from` membership test already proves whose balance fell) or allow it when any qualifying Transfer log has `from` in depositorAddresses.

findings.title: CHAT_ADMIN_KEY compared with === and bypasses the per-author rate limit
findings.description: The script key is compared with a plain string equality (not constant-time) and a caller presenting it skips both identity resolution and the slow_down limiter, so a leaked or guessed key allows unlimited announcements as 'EGREGORE'.
findings.fix: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual over equal-length buffers and apply a modest per-key rate limit.

findings.title: Server claimTimeout lets a defender who is stalling in the blockers stage take the win
findings.description: claimTimeout only checks that the caller is not ctx.currentPlayer and that turnDeadline + 60s has passed. After confirmAttackers the attacker is still currentPlayer but is parked in 'afk' with no way to progress; the defender holds priority in 'blockers' (an undeclared stage, so phase moves apply, including claimTimeout). A defender who simply never blocks can, 150s after the attacker's turn began, call claimTimeout and set the ATTACKER's life to 0 with reason 'timeout'. The attacker's only escape is forceEndTurn, i.e. cancelling their own attack. This is the server-only copy, so it directly affects ranked and wager results.
findings.fix: Make the timeout target 'whoever holds priority' rather than ctx.currentPlayer: while G.combat.attackers is non-empty the defender is the one on the clock, so claimTimeout should only be callable by the attacker against the defender (and vice versa otherwise). Reset the deadline on confirmAttackers.

findings.title: Draw effects run optimistically on the client against the stripped deck and zero the player's life
findings.description: playerView wipes G.secret.decks[pid] to [] before sending state to each client. boardgame.io's SocketIO client (App.tsx:6370) runs every move locally as an optimistic update unless the move sets `client: false`. playCard with drawTwo / on_meme_etb_draw / etb_zap_2_and_draw calls drawCard, which sees deck.length === 0 and sets life to 0 plus a 'loses' log line. Verified with CreateGameReducer({isClient:true}) on a playerView'd state: casting Study Session dropped the caster's life to 0 and appended 'tried to draw from empty deck and loses' until the server's authoritative update would replace the state. Every card draw online therefore flashes a self-loss (life 0, log line) and any gameover-driven UI (Board.tsx:888 effect, haptics, daily-win flag) can fire on the stale local state.
findings.fix: Declare playCard (and any move that reads G.secret) as `{ move: playCard, client: false }` so it only executes on the master, per boardgame.io's secret-state guidance; alternatively have drawCard consult the public deckCounts and never derive a loss on the client.

findings.title: InstallPrompt reads localStorage without try/catch inside an effect
findings.description: Every other storage access in the file is wrapped (the `local`/`sess` helpers, BgMusic, Settings.readFlag), but InstallPrompt calls localStorage.getItem bare. In Safari private mode with storage blocked, in some in-app browsers, or when the site is embedded with storage partitioning disabled, that throws SecurityError inside useEffect, which React treats as an uncaught render-phase error and unmounts the tree (see frontend-13). InstallPrompt is mounted on every signed-in screen, so the whole app would die for those users.
findings.fix: Use the existing `local.get` helper (or wrap in try/catch) and treat a storage failure as 'not dismissed'.

findings.title: Defender can cancel an in-progress attack with forceEndTurn once the 90s deadline lapses
findings.description: turnDeadline is set once in turn.onBegin and never refreshed when the attacker confirms attackers. The 'blockers' stage is not declared in turn.stages, so the defender falls through to the play-phase move list, which includes forceEndTurn. Scenario: attacker thinks for 85s, declares and confirms a lethal attack; the defender waits 5s and calls forceEndTurn, which wipes G.combat.attackers and ends the attacker's turn with zero damage dealt. Verified via the reducer: after confirmAttackers, forceEndTurn from the defender with turnDeadline in the past ended the turn, defender life unchanged, attackers=[]. In ranked/wager this is a free Fog every turn against a slow opponent; the attacker (parked in 'afk') can equally cancel their own confirmed attack.
findings.fix: When attackers are confirmed, give the defender their own block deadline and have a lapsed block deadline resolve combat with no blocks (call resolveCombat) instead of discarding it. Only the non-stalling side should be able to force-end, and forceEndTurn should not be reachable while G.combat.attackers is non-empty unless it resolves combat first.

findings.title: etb_zap_2_and_draw bypasses dealDamageToPlayer, so it is unlogged and skips any damage hooks
findings.description: Sproto Gremlin's ETB subtracts life directly instead of calling dealDamageToPlayer, so the standard 'Player X takes N damage (life=...)' log line is missing and any future hook on player damage (prevention, lifelink-style triggers, on-chain result reasons) will silently miss it. The log line it does emit is appended after drawCard, so a mill-out loss from that draw is logged before the zap that caused the turn.
findings.fix: Call dealDamageToPlayer(G, oppId, 2) and keep all player-life changes behind that helper.

findings.title: DeckWorkspace and ProfilePage loaders have no cancellation and race on identity change
findings.description: DeckWorkspace's mount effect awaits listDecksApi and then calls setDecks/loadInto/setStatus/setLoading with no `cancelled` flag, and ProfilePage's loader (2876-2886) does the same across three sequential awaits. If myName changes (profile rename via announceProfileChanged) or the tab is switched away before the response lands, the stale response overwrites the newer state or sets state on an unmounted component; loadInto() can reset the player's in-progress edits to the server copy. Landing, Lobby, SoloSetupModal and PublicProfile all do use the alive/cancelled pattern, so this is an inconsistency.
findings.fix: Add `let cancelled = false; ... return () => { cancelled = true; }` to both effects and bail before each setState, or move the loads into a shared `useAsync` hook.

findings.title: Module-level _uid counter: non-deterministic across client/master and resets on server restart
findings.description: Instance uids come from a process-global counter outside G. On the master the counter is shared by every match in the process and starts at 0 on each boot; the game service persists matches in bgio-postgres (new-backend/services/game/src/bgio/store.ts), so after a restart a resumed match keeps instances like 'c5' while the fresh counter issues 'c1','c2',... and eventually 'c5' again. findOnBattlefield / aurasOn / destroyMeme match by uid, so a collision silently targets or destroys the wrong permanent. On the client the counter also differs from the master's, so optimistic plays create uids the server never sees; a page reload mid-match restarts the client counter at 0 and can collide with live server uids.
findings.fix: Store the counter in G (e.g. G.nextUid) and have mkInstance read/increment it, so uids are deterministic and survive persistence; or derive uids from random.Die/ctx-based sequence inside the move.

findings.title: Every response is an unchecked `JSON.parse(...) as T`; shape drift crashes callers
findings.description: `parseBody` casts the parsed JSON to `T` with no runtime validation, and modules then destructure immediately (`const { escrow } = await post<{escrow: Escrow}>(...)`, `const { matches } = await get<...>`). A shape change yields `undefined` fields or a `TypeError: Cannot destructure` far from the fetch, with no `ApiError`. `ranked.ts:1005-1018` records exactly this already happening (`/games/ranked/me` not wrapped as expected, badge rendered RANK UNAVAILABLE). Only `collection.ts` and `addresses.listAddresses` normalise defensively.
findings.fix: Give `request()` an optional `parse: (raw: unknown) => T` (zod or hand-written guards like `normaliseView`) and throw `ApiError{code:'invalid_response'}` on mismatch, at least for the money/match-critical routes.

findings.title: evm-deploy.mjs overwrites deployment.json wholesale and is not reproducible against foundry.toml
findings.description: The script writes a fresh `result` object to contracts/deployment.json without merging, so re-running it would erase cardPack/cardPackPriceEth/cardCount/rpcNote added later by evm-deploy-pack.mjs. It hardcodes operator and feeRecipient to the deployer (the H-4 single-key setup) rather than reading env like Deploy.s.sol does. It compiles with whatever `solc` npm resolves (solc is not in package.json and node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts is absent in this checkout), not the 0.8.24/200-runs pinned in foundry.toml, so the deployed bytecode cannot be reproduced or verified from the Foundry project.
findings.fix: Delete the solc-js scripts and deploy only via `forge script` (pinned compiler, broadcast artifacts under contracts/broadcast), reading OPERATOR/FEE_RECIPIENT from env; if the script stays, merge into the existing JSON and pin solc to 0.8.24.

findings.title: collectRegions queries region='' so it always falls back to a hard-coded list
findings.description: listQueueForRegion('') matches rows whose region is the empty string, which never exist, so `all` is always empty and the matchmaker only ever scans 'na','eu','ap','global'. Any other region a client sends to /api/ranked/queue/join (String(body.region) is unvalidated) strands that player in a shard that is never scanned.
findings.fix: Use `SELECT DISTINCT region FROM ranked_queue` and validate region against a fixed enum at join time.

findings.title: Cross-tab `storage` handler JSON.parses unguarded
findings.description: The `storage` event listener parses `e.newValue` directly. The surrounding try/catch wraps only the `addEventListener` call, not the callback, so a non-JSON value written under `chains.session.v1` by another tab, an extension or a devtools edit throws an uncaught exception inside the auth layer in every other open tab.
findings.fix: Wrap the parse in try/catch and treat an unparseable value as `null` (signed out).

findings.title: Signer is `globalThis.ethereum`, not the provider that connected; EIP-6963 ignored
findings.description: `connectRobinhoodChain()` requests accounts from `window.ethereum`, and `signMessageEvm` separately grabs `globalThis.ethereum` to `personal_sign`. With several injected wallets (MetaMask + Rabby + Coinbase, common on Robinhood Chain users' browsers) `window.ethereum` is whichever extension won the injection race; the connected account and the signing provider can differ, giving the server a signature from a different key and a 401 'signature not accepted' that the UI blames on an expired challenge (`runtime.tsx:220`). None of the wallet code uses EIP-6963 `eip6963:announceProvider` discovery.
findings.fix: Have `connectRobinhoodChain()` return the provider it used and pass it into `signMessageEvm`; discover providers via EIP-6963 and let the user pick when more than one is present.

findings.title: Presence heartbeat bypasses the HTTP wrapper and dies with the access token
findings.description: `beat()` builds its own `fetch` with a raw `Authorization` header from `getAccessToken()`, outside `src/api/http.ts`, so it gets no 401-refresh, no timeout and no `ApiError`. Access tokens live 15 minutes; a player idling on the hub with no other traffic will 401 on every beat after that and silently drop out of the "players online" count while still being online. It also forwards the bearer token to a second service (the Vercel function) that is not the gateway, widening where the credential travels.
findings.fix: Either route the heartbeat through `request()` with an absolute path override (so a 401 refreshes once), or call `refreshSession()` when `res.status === 401` before giving up.

findings.title: Legacy POST /api/ranked/match/result is public and ingests any outcome
findings.description: The route is commented 'Server-internal' but is mounted on the same public Koa middleware with no auth check, so any caller can post {matchId, seasonId, player0, player1, winner} and move two arbitrary players' Glicko ratings and LP. matchId idempotency only stops the same id being replayed, not new fabricated ids.
findings.fix: Remove the HTTP surface; call ingestMatchResult only from server code that reads the authoritative boardgame.io gameover (new-backend's apply-result.ts runs inside the result-recording transaction).

findings.title: Hand-size discard pops from the end of the hand with no player choice
findings.description: passTurn (and forceEndTurn at line 718) discards down to 7 by `hand.pop()`, i.e. the most recently drawn cards, with no choice offered. Verified: a 9-card hand ending in 'base_based' discarded ['base_based','base_degen']. Drawing into a bomb with Revelation/Study Session and then passing throws the bomb away; the player has no move to pick discards. This is a rules gap, not just UX, because the hand order is an implementation detail (drawCard pushes to the end, bounce pushes to the end).
findings.fix: Either add a `discardCard(handIndex)` move and block passTurn while hand.length > 7, or at minimum discard from the front (oldest) and document it; add a test either way.

findings.title: First player always draws on turn one: ctx.turn is never 1 in the play phase
findings.description: turn.onBegin skips the draw only when ctx.turn === 1, but boardgame.io increments ctx.turn on every StartTurn, including the one that opens each phase. The pick and mulligan phases consume turn 1 (and 2 when the pick phase is live), so the play phase opens at ctx.turn 2 or 3 and the starting player draws to 8 cards. Verified by driving the reducer: after both keepHand calls, ctx.phase='play', ctx.turn=2, starting player hand=8, other hand=7. Side effects: the starting seat gets the MTG 'play AND draw' double advantage, the log/Board show 'Turn 2' for the first turn, and because the phase transitions eat a turn each, seat '1' (the joiner) moves first whenever colors are preset via setupData.
findings.evidence:
// Draw (skip on the very first turn of the game for the starting player)
      if (ctx.turn !== 1) drawCard(G, ctx.currentPlayer, 1);
findings.fix: Track the first play turn in G (e.g. `G.firstPlayTurn ??= ctx.turn` in phases.play.onBegin) and skip the draw when `ctx.turn === G.firstPlayTurn`, or keep a `turnsPlayed` counter in G. Add a reducer-level test asserting the starting hand stays at 7.

findings.title: Bot uses Math.random, so the seeded Daily Challenge is not reproducible
findings.description: dailyChallenge.ts promises 'same RNG seed + same bot color for every player who plays on a given UTC date', and MMTCGBot forwards `seed` to boardgame.io's Bot base, which exposes a seeded `this.random`. But _compute picks the color with Math.random (line 239), the Easy policy picks moves with Math.random (line 317), and play() jitters with Math.random (line 228). The game RNG is seeded, the bot is not, so two players with identical seeds and decks get different bot behaviour and the daily leaderboard compares unlike games. dailyBotColor() is also computed but the bot ignores it when it picks its own color.
findings.fix: Use `this.random()` (seeded by the Bot base) for the color and the Easy move pick, and keep Math.random only for the cosmetic delay.

findings.title: Damage moves accept any non-empty targetUid; a stale or bogus uid eats the card and gas with no effect
findings.description: For damage2/3/5 the pre-pay validation only checks `!targetUid`. If the uid is not '__p0__'/'__p1__' and findOnBattlefield fails (meme already died, typo from the UI, or a node/machine uid), pay() and the hand splice still run and the switch silently does nothing. Verified: playCard(0, 'nonexistent-uid') with Cheap Shot removed the card, spent 1 sol gas and put the card in the graveyard with no damage dealt. The same code path also allows targeting a node or machine uid, which fizzles identically.
findings.fix: Before paying, resolve the target: accept '__p0__'/'__p1__' or a uid whose findOnBattlefield zone is 'memes'; otherwise return INVALID_MOVE.

findings.title: No CI workflow and no lint/format configuration anywhere in the repo
findings.description: There is no .github/workflows directory in the root or in new-backend/, and no eslint, prettier, biome or editorconfig file. Combined with hygiene-01 (red test suite) and hygiene-07 (unchecked server code), nothing runs tsc, vitest or a build before a push lands on main and Vercel auto-deploys it. Style drift across 7,000+ line files like App.tsx is also unchecked.
findings.evidence:
$ ls .github new-backend/.github
ls: cannot access '.github': No such file or directory
$ ls -a | grep -iE 'eslint|prettier|biome|editorconfig'
(none)
findings.fix: Add a single GitHub Actions workflow running `npm ci && npx tsc -b && npx vitest run && npx vite build` on PRs (plus `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test` in new-backend/), and adopt biome or eslint+prettier with a `lint` script.

findings.title: POST /games/create accepts mode 'ranked', enabling win-trading outside the queue
findings.description: CreateBody allows mode: 'ranked' together with invitedDisplayName, so two colluding accounts can create private ranked matches against each other at will, and the recorder rates them exactly like queue matches (applyRankedResult runs on `mode = 'ranked'` from game.matches). This bypasses the matchmaker's rating window, lets a player farm LP against a throwaway account, and ranked.repo.ts itself notes 'nothing stops a profile holding two live ranked matches created through POST /games/create'.
findings.evidence:
const CreateBody = strictBody({
  mode: z.enum(['casual', 'ranked', 'wager']).default('casual'),
  ...
  invitedDisplayName: zDisplayName.optional(),
...
const match = await insertOpenMatch({
  id: randomUUID(),
  mode: body.mode as MatchMode,
findings.fix: Restrict CreateBody.mode to 'casual' | 'wager' so ranked matches can only be minted by the matchmaker (insertLiveRankedMatch), or at minimum refuse ranked + invitedDisplayName.

findings.title: starterDeck() truncation silently drops every aura (and Arcane Storm) from the starters
findings.description: The builder appends 22 nodes + 3x memes + 2x machines/moves/auras, then `.slice(0, 60)`. With 8 memes, 4 machines, 3 moves and 1 aura that is 62 cards, so the last two entries, the two aura copies, are cut from all five starters. Knowledge has 9 memes (65 cards) and additionally loses both Arcane Storm copies and one Banish. Verified by tallying STARTER_DECKS: bnb/sol/eth/robinhood each lack their aura; base lacks base_airdrop and base_staybased and has base_bridge x1. Nobody playing a starter ever sees the aura mechanic, and the doc comment ('~22 nodes + 3 of each Meme + 2 of each Machine/Move') predates auras.
findings.fix: Compute the node count as 60 minus the spell count (clamped), or trim surplus from the node pile / meme triplicates instead of the tail. Add a cards.test assertion that every non-node card of a color appears in its starter.

findings.title: Client-side 60 s turn timer resets on every parent render and on blocker phases
findings.description: TurnBanner's interval depends on `onEndTurn`, which ChainsBoard passes as a fresh inline arrow (`() => { Haptics.turn(); moves.passTurn(); }`), so the interval is torn down and recreated on every board render, losing up to a second of countdown each time. The reset effect also depends on `canEndTurn`, which flips false/true whenever the opponent enters and leaves the blockers stage, so the displayed timer jumps back to 60 after each combat. The TURN_LIMIT constant is independent of the server's G.turnDeadline that the same component uses for the force-end button, so the two clocks shown to the two players disagree.
findings.fix: Drive the visible countdown from G.turnDeadline (the server clock) exactly as the force-end path does, hold onEndTurn in a ref, and reset only on `[turn, myTurn]`.

findings.title: Escrow signing key is a plaintext env var in a container on a shared host
findings.description: WAGER_ESCROW_KEYPAIR is loaded from the environment and held in process memory; DEPLOY.md confirms it lives in /opt/chains-tcg/.env on a root-SSH host shared with another project, and INTEGRATION.md §9 lists this as the top risk. Every player stake is drainable by anyone with the env, a container shell, or a compose file copy. The current keys are documented placeholders, so this is a pre-launch blocker rather than a live loss.
findings.fix: Move signing behind a KMS/HSM signer with a per-tx policy (or deploy an escrow contract) before funding the wallet; at minimum isolate the host and rotate the placeholder keys.

findings.title: Legacy ranked queue accepts a client-supplied deck list as `deckId`
findings.description: joinQueue parses `selectedDeckId` as a JSON array of card ids and uses it as the player's deck for the ranked match. Only format legality (validateDeck) is checked, never ownership or that it equals a saved deck, so a ranked player can bring any 60 cards from the catalogue. The matchmaker then passes these straight into setupData.decks.
findings.fix: Resolve the deck server-side from the player's active deck and check ownership at enqueue and at pairing, as new-backend/services/game/src/ranked/queue.ts does.

findings.title: Anyone can burn a victim's pending sign-in challenge via POST /auth/verify
findings.description: consumeNonce does GETDEL on the per-(chain,address) key before any signature is checked, and /auth/verify is public. An attacker who knows a target wallet address can POST /auth/verify with that address and a garbage signature while the victim is signing, destroying the challenge so the victim's real verify fails with 'No active sign-in challenge'. Repeating this within the per-address limits (10/min) is enough to keep a specific player from logging in. Issuing a new nonce for the address likewise overwrites the victim's outstanding one.
findings.fix: Key the Redis record by the nonce value (which only the requester's browser holds) rather than by address, or verify the signature against the stored message before deleting and only consume on success (keeping a short replay-blacklist for used nonces).

findings.title: refreshCollection applies a response under whichever wallet is signed in when it returns
findings.description: refreshCollection captures nothing about the identity it was issued for; applyServerSnapshot writes to cacheKey() and the live `confirmed` map at response time. If the user signs out and into a different wallet while GET /wager/collection is in flight (onSessionChange calls resetForIdentity, then a fresh refresh), the earlier response lands after the reset and overwrites wallet B's snapshot and localStorage cache with wallet A's cards, which the deck builder then treats as authoritative until the next refresh. `inFlight` dedupes concurrent calls but does not cancel the stale one.
findings.fix: Capture `const address = currentAddress()` before the request and drop the response if currentAddress() differs afterwards (also clear inFlight in resetForIdentity).

findings.title: Waiting room fetches a public profile literally named 'Opponent'
findings.description: The players memo fills the other seat with the placeholder name 'Opponent' once the seat is full, and the avatar effect then calls getProfileApi for every named player. That issues GET /api/profiles/Opponent on every match start (a guaranteed 404, or worse, a real player who registered the display name 'Opponent' gets their avatar shown as the opponent). The seat response carries no opponent name, so the request can never succeed legitimately.
findings.fix: Mark the placeholder seat with a flag (e.g. `{ id, placeholder: true }`) and skip the profile fetch for it, or only fetch for `myName`; also guard the .then with the existing alive pattern so a late response does not setState after unmount.

findings.title: config.ts comments contradict the shipped env: `/gw` proxy, tracked `.env.production`
findings.description: The header says `.env.production` sets `VITE_API_BASE=https://api.ocva.online` and line 674 says `.env.production is git-ignored`; in fact it is tracked (`git ls-files` lists it, `.gitignore` has `!.env.production`) and sets `VITE_API_BASE=/gw` via the Vercel rewrite. `defaultBase()` and the `SOCKET_URL` fallback also hardcode `https://api.ocva.online` in source, so a staging deployment that forgets the env var silently talks to production. Someone following the comment will debug the wrong thing.
findings.fix: Update the comments to describe `/gw` + `VITE_SOCKET_URL`, and fail loudly (throw at module init) when neither `VITE_API_BASE` nor a localhost origin is present rather than defaulting to prod.

findings.title: 429 retry ignores body `retryAfterSec`, retrying after 1s against a long limit
findings.description: `errors.ts:828-836` documents that the rate limiter puts the delay in the body as `details.retryAfterSec` and `toApiError` honours it. The retry loop in `request()` reads only the `Retry-After` header, discards the body (`res.text()`), and falls back to `DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT_MS = 1000`. When the gateway signals a 30s limit in the body only, the client fires two more requests one second apart (deepening the limit) and then throws `Rate limited. Try again in ? seconds.` with `retryAfter: null`, so `errorText` cannot tell the player how long to wait.
findings.fix: Parse the 429 body once (reuse `toApiError`) and take `err.retryAfter` (header or body) for both the sleep and the thrown error.

findings.title: `as any` escape hatches hide untyped game state and events
findings.description: The board reads `(G as any).deckCounts` because GState does not declare deckCounts; WagerPayoutModal and WinnerShareModal take `gameover: any`; CombatStrip takes `ctx: any`; TurnBanner takes `myProfile?: any`. App's solo-end listener is `function onEnd(e: any)`, InstallPrompt is `useState<any>`, share uses `(navigator as any).share`, SoloClient casts `ChainsTCG.setup as any` and `ChainsBoard as any`, Boosters has `(window as any).ethereum` and `mapMintError(e: any)`. Each one is a place where a server/game-shape change compiles cleanly and fails at runtime (e.g. a renamed deckCounts silently shows 'Deck (0)').
findings.fix: Add deckCounts to GState, type gameover as `Ctx['gameover']` with a local `GameOver = { winner?: string; draw?: boolean }`, type ctx as boardgame.io `Ctx`, and declare `window.ethereum` / `navigator.share` in vite-env.d.ts.

findings.title: Legacy pairing handoff is an in-process Map that is consumed on read
findings.description: Pairings live in `pendingByPlayer` and takePendingMatchFor deletes the entry when the status poll returns it. A poll that races a page reload, a second tab, or a restart loses the match id permanently while both players have already been dequeued, so they are stuck. When the LobbyClient createMatch call fails the code also fabricates a 'ranked-...' id that corresponds to no boardgame.io match.
findings.fix: Persist the pairing as a real match row and let the status endpoint read it idempotently (new-backend writes game.matches live and answers GET /games/ranked/queue from it).

findings.title: No default timeout on any API fetch; a stalled gateway wedges the UI
findings.description: `request()` forwards only the caller-supplied `signal`; most call sites pass none (e.g. lobby.create, decks.activate, auth.verifySignature). There is no AbortController/timeout, so a hung Vercel rewrite or gateway connection leaves spinners (sign-in, deck activate, queue join) pending indefinitely with no error to show. The 429 path bounds its *wait* (`MAX_RETRY_WAIT_MS`) but nothing bounds the fetch itself.
findings.fix: Combine `options.signal` with `AbortSignal.timeout(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS)` (or `AbortSignal.any`) inside `request()`, surfacing the timeout as `ApiError{code:'timeout'}`.

findings.title: Live-match check in joinQueue is TOCTOU; pairer never excludes seated players
findings.description: joinQueue reads liveRankedMatchFor outside the transaction and repo.enqueue runs after it, so a player paired between the check and the INSERT ends up both seated and queued. pairOnce (matchmaker.ts) claims queue rows without checking game.matches, so the next tick can seat the same profile in a second live ranked match. Ratings stay consistent thanks to lockStanding ordering, but one of the two matches will time out or be conceded, costing the player LP.
findings.fix: Do the live-match check and the enqueue in one transaction, and have claimSeed/claimOpponent exclude profiles with a live ranked match via NOT EXISTS on game.matches.

findings.title: In-match 'FORFEIT & LEAVE' never forfeits: it just unmounts the client
findings.description: doLeave() calls lobbyApi.cancel, which the code itself notes is a 404 for any match already in progress, and then calls onLeave() which only clears the local seat. No concede/forfeit move exists in Game.ts (grep for concede|forfeit|surrender|resign returns nothing), so the dialog headline 'Forfeit this match?' and the button 'FORFEIT & LEAVE' promise an outcome the server never receives. The opponent is left on 'disconnected — waiting to reconnect' and has to force-end every one of the leaver's turns until they deck out; the leaver's W/L is not updated at the moment they believe they conceded.
findings.fix: Add a server-validated `concede` move to Game.ts and have MatchSeat (or Board) call it when the match is live before releasing the seat; until then change the copy to 'Leave match (you stay seated; the opponent can force-end your turns)' so the UI does not claim a forfeit.

findings.title: Clickable cards and map sites are not real buttons
findings.description: HubCardTile is a focusable div with onKeyDown/onDoubleClick but no role, so assistive tech announces it as a group of text; its '+' key shortcut is undiscoverable. MasterquestPage renders each site as an SVG <g onClick> with no tabIndex, role or key handler, so the campaign cannot be played from the keyboard at all. Board's CardFace/MiniCard do set role=button and tabIndex, which shows the team knows the pattern.
findings.evidence:
<div className="hub-anim" tabIndex={showAdd ? 0 : -1}
        onKeyDown={(e) => { if (showAdd && onAdd && !disabled && (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === '+')) { e.preventDefault(); onAdd(); } }}
        onDoubleClick={() => { if (showAdd && onAdd && !disabled) onAdd(); }}
  ...
          <g key={s.id}
            onClick={() => onSiteClick(s)}
            style={{ cursor: (cleared || unlocked) ? 'pointer' : 'not-allowed' }}>
findings.fix: Give HubCardTile role="button" and an aria-label (or make the whole tile a <button>), and give each Masterquest <g> tabIndex=0, role="button", aria-label=`Site N: name` and an Enter/Space handler.

findings.title: Plaza canvas lobby is unreachable: plazaOpen is never set to true
findings.description: Lobby keeps `plazaOpen` state and renders <Plaza> when it is true, but the only setter calls are setPlazaOpen(false). The 'Enter Plaza' button instead window.open()s an external WorkAdventure URL. The 276-line src/Plaza.tsx (its own rAF loop, keyboard handlers and canvas renderer) is therefore shipped but dead, and the hard-coded third-party URL is the real behaviour.
findings.fix: Either wire the button to setPlazaOpen(true) and drop the external URL, or delete plazaOpen, the <Plaza> branch and src/Plaza.tsx and move the WorkAdventure URL into config.

findings.title: `ensureChain` swallows switch failures; mint can proceed on the wrong network
findings.description: `ensureChain()` catches every error from `wallet_switchEthereumChain` and only acts on code 4902; a user rejection (4001) or a wallet that ignores the request is silently swallowed, and `mintPack()` goes straight on to `writeContract`. There is no `eth_chainId` read-back (unlike `wallet.ts:connectRobinhoodChain`, which was written specifically because `wallet_addEthereumChain` can resolve without switching). Depending on the wallet, viem either throws a confusing chain-mismatch error or the wallet prompts a 0.0035 ETH send to `CARD_PACK` on whatever chain it is on. Currently dormant (`PACK_MINTING_AVAILABLE = false`) but it is the live mint path when re-enabled.
findings.fix: Reuse `connectRobinhoodChain()` from wallet.ts (which rethrows rejections and reads `eth_chainId` back) and refuse to call `writeContract` unless the confirmed chain id is 4663.

findings.title: App() returns before any hook when ?print is set (rules-of-hooks violation)
findings.description: The print-mode early return sits above 14 useState and 10 useEffect calls. It is stable per mount today (the URL does not change under React), so it does not crash, but it is a rules-of-hooks violation that eslint-plugin-react-hooks flags and that will break the moment printMode becomes reactive (e.g. hashchange). It also means the print renderer inherits none of the session handling.
findings.fix: Decide print mode in index.tsx and mount <PrintAllCards /> instead of <App /> there, or move the check into a tiny wrapper component so App's hook order is unconditional.

findings.title: 'Remember me' is silently undone on every page load
findings.description: `remember` is initialised to `false` (App.tsx:278) and an effect calls `setPersistence(remember ? 'local' : 'session')` on mount. `session.ts` hydrates the saved mode `'local'` and restores the session from localStorage, then this effect immediately flips the mode back to `'session'`, overwrites `chains.session.persistence.v1`, and `writeThrough()` removes the localStorage copy. A player who ticked Remember-me gets exactly one more page load out of it; a new tab or a browser restart after that demands a fresh wallet signature, which is the opposite of what the checkbox promised.
findings.fix: Initialise `remember` from `sessionApi.getPersistence() === 'local'` and only call `setPersistence` from the checkbox's onChange (or when a sign-in starts), not from a mount effect.

findings.title: enumerateMoves never offers a second declareAttacker, so Easy/MCTS attacks with at most one meme
findings.description: `inBlock` is computed as `G.combat.attackers.length > 0`, which is true as soon as the first attacker is declared (not only during the blockers stage). Once one meme is declared the enumerator only offers confirmAttackers, so the Easy bot (and anything using Game.ai.enumerate) can never swing with two or more memes. The Normal/Hard policy bypasses the enumerator so it is unaffected, which hides the bug.
findings.fix: Detect the blockers stage from ctx.activePlayers (or the attacker being in 'afk') instead of the attacker count, and keep enumerating declareAttacker for undeclared memes.

findings.title: Result reporting is correctly server-owned; only the daily-quest flag is client-trusted
findings.description: Verified: Board.tsx no longer POSTs any result, winner or payout instruction (the gameover effect only does haptics, a localStorage flag and the solo-end event), and MatchSeat/Lobby never send a deck or seat. The one remaining client-trusted outcome is the 'Win 1 match' daily quest: Board writes `ocva.daily.<date>.win` to localStorage and ActivityPanel (App 2504) reads it, so anyone can tick the quest from devtools. That is harmless while the quest is cosmetic, but it must never be wired to a reward without moving the check server-side. Also note the auto-pass (782) and force-end (3029, 2872) moves are client-initiated from local clocks; they are only safe because the server validates the moves.
findings.fix: Leave as is, but add a comment on ActivityPanel that the quest is cosmetic and client-trusted, and derive it from match history (GET /api/matches) if it ever gates a reward.

findings.title: `mintTicketNft` retries across RPCs on any error, risking a double mint
findings.description: The mint loop treats every exception, including a confirmation timeout after the transaction was already broadcast, as 'try the next RPC'. A `sendAndConfirm` that times out on RPC A may still land, after which the same `ticketNumber` is minted again via RPC B with a fresh asset signer, producing two Core NFTs for one payment (and the treasury pays rent twice). Only the second mint address is recorded.
findings.fix: Generate the asset signer once outside the loop and, on a timeout, check whether that asset already exists (`fetchAsset`) before re-sending; only rotate RPCs on pre-broadcast failures (auth/rate-limit).

findings.title: 'blockers' stage is never declared; defender's move set relies on boardgame.io fallthrough
findings.description: confirmAttackers sets the defender to stage 'blockers', but turn.stages only defines 'afk'. boardgame.io's GetMove treats an undefined stage as 'use the phase moves', so the defender gets every play-phase move (playCard, tapNode, passTurn, forceEndTurn...) and the game depends on each move's own `ctx.currentPlayer` guard to reject them. This is the root enabler of engine-02 and means any new phase move is automatically exposed to the blocking player. It also makes the Board's `inBlockers` logic depend on a string that exists nowhere in the game config.
findings.fix: Declare `blockers: { moves: { declareBlocker, confirmBlocks } }` in turn.stages and reference the stage name through a shared constant used by Game.ts, bot.ts and Board.tsx.

findings.title: No error boundary anywhere above the board: one render error blanks the whole app
findings.description: index.tsx mounts <App /> directly and the only componentDidCatch in the codebase is inside privy/runtime.tsx. Any thrown render error (e.g. CARDS[id] undefined for an unknown card id in CurrentDeckPanel line 4010 `CARDS[id].name`, or an unexpected gameover shape in Board) unmounts the entire tree, including a live boardgame.io socket client, and leaves a white page with no way back except reload. Mid-match that reads as a crash and a dropped game.
findings.evidence: createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
findings.fix: Wrap <App /> in a root ErrorBoundary that renders a 'Something broke — reload / back to hub' panel and logs the error, and add a second boundary around <ChainsClient> in MatchSeat/SoloClient so a board error does not tear down the session.

findings.title: Booster price is documented as 0.0035 ETH but charged as 0.0035 SOL; two 'MASTER' tokens with 18 vs 6 decimals
findings.description: booster-mint.ts says BOOSTER_PRICE_SOL is 'denominated in ETH for Robinhood Chain' yet converts it to lamports and charges that many SOL on Solana, a roughly 15x price difference versus the CardPack's 0.0035 ETH; the two pack products share one number in different units. Separately, MasterToken.sol is an 18-decimal ERC-20 on Robinhood Chain while wager-program.ts/server-custodial.ts treat $MASTER as a 6-decimal pump.fun SPL mint; contracts/README.md says RAKE_BPS 'matches CUSTODIAL_BURN_BPS' as if they were one system. Any future cross-wiring (e.g. reusing masterUi for the EVM token) would be off by 10^12.
findings.fix: Name the env by its real unit (BOOSTER_PRICE_SOL vs CARD_PACK_PRICE_ETH), set them independently, and rename one of the two tokens/constants (e.g. MASTER_EVM_DECIMALS = 18) so the decimals cannot be conflated.

findings.title: A required call while signed out clears the (absent) session and resets the whole UI
findings.description: When a `auth: 'required'` request 401s and `getSession()` is null, `request()` calls `clearSession()` and throws `SessionExpiredError`. `clearSession()` emits to every `onSessionChange` subscriber even though nothing changed, and App.tsx:7181-7197 responds by wiping seat/view/profile state and jumping to `landing`. Any component that calls an authenticated route optimistically while signed out (e.g. a collection or ticket read on a public page) therefore yanks the player off the screen they were on instead of just receiving an error.
findings.fix: Skip `clearSession()` when there was no session to begin with (just throw), or make `clearSession()` a no-op that does not `emit()` when `current` is already null.

findings.title: rules-intro.mp4 is referenced in 3 places but excluded from the Vercel deploy
findings.description: .vercelignore drops public/rules-intro.mp4 (172 MB, over Vercel's static limit) with the note that it is 'served from the Render deployment instead', but src/App.tsx and src/Board.tsx hard-code the relative path `/rules-intro.mp4` with no fallback host. The file is also a Git LFS object, so a Vercel build from git gets a pointer file unless LFS is enabled. On egregoretcg.xyz the rules video element therefore 404s or plays a 130-byte pointer; the comment's Render fallback no longer matches where the backend lives (new-backend/DEPLOY.md: Docker on a VPS behind Caddy).
findings.evidence:

# Exceeds Vercel's static file-size limit (~172 MB). Served from the Render
# deployment instead; on Vercel the rules-intro video simply won't load.
public/rules-intro.mp4
$ grep -rn 'rules-intro.mp4' src
src/App.tsx:900:            src="/rules-intro.mp4"
src/App.tsx:1759:      <video ref={vidRef} src="/rules-intro.mp4" poster="/intro.png" ...
src/Board.tsx:3219:            src="/rules-intro.mp4"
$ cat .gitattributes
*.mp4 filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text
$ ls -la public/rules-intro.mp4
180432291 public/rules-intro.mp4
findings.fix: Host the video on object storage/CDN (or re-encode it well under 100 MB) and reference it through a `VITE_RULES_VIDEO_URL` env var; remove it from the repo and from LFS.

findings.title: initialize is permissionless: whoever calls it first after deploy becomes admin and picks the oracle
findings.description: Initialize has no constraint tying admin to the program upgrade authority or a hardcoded pubkey; the only guard is that the Config PDA can be created once. DEPLOY.md performs `solana program deploy` and `initialize.ts` as separate steps on mainnet, so a watcher can front-run the init with their own oracle/admin, after which set_config is theirs (has_one = admin) and the deployer must redeploy under a new program id. Low likelihood but total impact for the program.
findings.evidence:
#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Initialize<'info> {
    #[account(mut)] pub admin: Signer<'info>,
    #[account(
        init,
        payer = admin,
        space = 8 + Config::SIZE,
        seeds = [CONFIG_SEED],
        bump,
    )]
    pub config: Account<'info, Config>,
findings.fix: Add `#[account(constraint = admin.key() == EXPECTED_ADMIN)]` or verify the signer against the program's upgrade authority via the ProgramData account, or bundle deploy+initialize in one transaction.

findings.title: burn_bps is read from Config at settle rather than snapshotted on the match
findings.description: Like the EVM rake issue, settle_match computes burn_amt from cfg.burn_bps at settlement time. The admin can raise burn_bps to the 20% cap via set_config right before an oracle settle of a large pot and lower it afterward; players agreed to 10% at join time. Bounded by MAX_BURN_BPS so impact is limited, but the Match struct already stores wager/mint and could store the rate.
findings.fix: Add burn_bps: u16 to Match, set it in create_match from cfg.burn_bps, and use m.burn_bps in settle_match.

findings.title: Card catalogue is duplicated in new-backend and has drifted by 405+ lines
findings.description: new-backend/services/game/src/game/cards.ts is a hand-vendored copy of src/cards.ts (its header says `DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` and `Re-sync with: cp ../../../src/cards.ts src/game/cards.ts`). Nothing enforces the sync: the committed copies already differ by 405 lines, and the uncommitted Wealth/Knowledge art additions push that to 445. The backend copy is what `validateDeck`, `CARDS`, `DECK_SIZE` and `derivePrimaryColor` run against for deck validation, so a card added or re-costed on the client can be accepted or rejected differently by the server.
findings.fix: Move the shared card data into a package both sides consume (e.g. new-backend/packages/cards published as a workspace, or generate a JSON catalogue from src/cards.ts at build time), and add a test or CI step that fails when the two files diverge beyond the documented one-line type fix.

findings.title: Mint sends a hardcoded price when the price read fails, and waits forever for the receipt
findings.description: `fetchPackPrice()` falls back to `parseEther('0.0035')` on any RPC failure, and `mintPack()` uses that as `value` with a fixed `gas: 1_500_000n` and no `simulateContract`. If the contract price has changed and the public RPC hiccups, the user signs a transaction that reverts on-chain and pays the gas. `waitForTransactionReceipt` is called without `timeout`, so viem polls indefinitely (its `timeout` is optional/undefined) and the pending state in `Boosters.tsx` never resolves if the hash is dropped from the mempool.
findings.fix: Make `fetchPackPrice` throw (block the buy with an error) instead of guessing; call `pub.simulateContract` before `writeContract`; pass `timeout` to `waitForTransactionReceipt` and surface a 'still pending, check Blockscout' state.

findings.title: Refresh fetch has no timeout and a network blip logs the user out
findings.description: `refreshSession()` is the single-flight promise every concurrent 401 awaits. The underlying `fetch` has no signal/timeout, so one hung `/auth/refresh` blocks every authenticated request in the app until the browser gives up. Worse, the `catch` treats *any* thrown error (offline, DNS, abort) as proof the token is dead and calls `clearSession()`, so a momentary connection drop on mobile forces a fresh wallet signature. The comment admits the trade-off, but a transient `TypeError: Failed to fetch` is distinguishable from a 401 and should not burn the session.
findings.fix: Add an `AbortSignal.timeout` to the refresh fetch; on a thrown network error return `false` WITHOUT clearing the session and let the caller surface a network error (the refresh token was never presented, so no family-revocation risk).

findings.title: Meme damage only clears when combat resolves, so post-combat damage persists for turns
findings.description: resolveCombat zeroes m.damage for every meme, but turn.onEnd does not. Damage dealt outside a resolved combat (Blinding Dawn / Arcane Storm cast in the second main phase, Firebomb/Cheap Shot/Punchline/Stampede on a meme, or combat damage from a turn where the defender force-ended) stays on the meme through the opponent's turn and until some later combat actually resolves. A 3/3 hit by Arcane Storm after combat is effectively a 3/2 for the rest of the game if no one attacks. MTG clears damage in every cleanup step.
findings.fix: Move the damage reset into turn.onEnd (and keep it after combat if desired). Also reset it in forceEndTurn's path, which currently clears attackers but not damage.

findings.title: render.yaml no longer matches the deployed backend and contradicts the README
findings.description: render.yaml still provisions a service named onchain-virtual-arena that boots the legacy Koa server (src/server.ts via `npm start`), with ALLOW_ORIGIN for masterstcg.com and env for HELIUS/MEMETIC_MASTERS/CUSTODIAL_ESCROW_KEYPAIR. Its comments say the DB is on Supabase while the README says Render provisions Postgres. The real backend per new-backend/DEPLOY.md is a nine-container Docker stack on a VPS behind Caddy at api.ocva.online. Anyone applying this blueprint stands up a second, stale backend with its own escrow keypair.
findings.evidence:
$ sed -n 9,14p render.yaml
  - type: web
    name: onchain-virtual-arena
    ...
    buildCommand: npm ci && npm run build
    startCommand: npm start
$ grep -n ALLOW_ORIGIN -A1 render.yaml | head -2
        value: "https://ocva.online,...,https://www.masterstcg.com,https://masterstcg.com"
$ sed -n 3,4p new-backend/DEPLOY.md
Deployed 2026-07-27. ... Nine containers: postgres, redis, migrate, auth, profile, game, wager, rpc-proxy, gateway.
$ grep -n 'npm start\|"start"' package.json
    "start": "tsx src/server.ts",
findings.fix: Delete render.yaml (and the `start`/`serve`/`dev:server` scripts plus koa-static if src/server.ts is truly retired), or mark it clearly as legacy and point deploy docs at new-backend/DEPLOY.md.

findings.title: Hand-strip ResizeObserver effect has no deps: re-created on every board render
findings.description: The effect that measures the mobile hand strip omits a dependency array, so every render of ChainsBoard (every G/ctx update, every notice, every selection) disconnects and constructs a new ResizeObserver and re-observes. ResizeObserver fires an initial callback on observe(), which calls setHandStripH; if the rounded height differs by even 1px from the previous render that triggers another render and another observer. On a phone during combat this is a steady churn of observer allocation and extra renders in the hottest component in the app.
findings.fix: Add `[mobile]` as the dependency array (the strip only exists on mobile) and guard the setter with `h => h === next ? h : next` to stop the measure/render loop.

findings.title: Uncommitted Wealth/Knowledge art map references 34 untracked WebP files
findings.description: On feature/sproto-factions, src/cards.ts has 40 uncommitted lines mapping robinhood_*/knowledge_* cards to /cards/wealth/*.webp and /cards/knowledge/*.webp, and docs/CARDS.txt and src/cards.test.ts are modified, while public/cards/knowledge (6.0 MB) and public/cards/wealth (4.6 MB, 34 files total) are untracked. If cards.ts is committed without `git add public/cards/{knowledge,wealth}`, the Vercel build from git renders every Wealth and Knowledge card with a 404 image.
