findings.fix: Commit the art and the catalogue change together, and add a cards.test.ts assertion that every CARD_ART path resolves to an existing file under public/ so a missing asset fails the suite.

findings.title: Ownership helpers answer from the editable localStorage cache before the server replies
findings.description: The module header promises the cached snapshot is 'never an input to a decision', but `resetForIdentity()` hydrates `confirmed` and `snapshotConfirmed` from `localStorage`, and `ownedCount`/`deckCap`/`ownershipIssues` read those directly. Until `refreshCollection()` lands, the deck builder caps copies and shows 'you do not own X' based on a value anyone can edit in devtools. The server still enforces ranked/wager seating, so this is not a security hole, but the client can show wrong caps/warnings and the comment is misleading for the next maintainer.
findings.fix: Track `source` alongside `confirmed` and have `ownershipKnown()` return false while `source === 'cache'`, or keep the cache for `cards` display only and not for `confirmed`.

findings.title: Payout idempotency-key conflict is only logged; escrow is finalised with the proposer's status
findings.description: When a payout row already exists for a different decision (e.g. an operator void raced the settlement worker), executePayout warns and continues: it takes the lease, ensureLegs is a no-op because the other decision's legs exist, Phase 3 drives those legs, and finalise() writes `plan.finalStatus` of the *proposer's* plan. A void refund can thus leave the escrow marked 'settled' (or a winner payout marked 'void'), corrupting the audit trail even though no double payment occurs.
findings.fix: Return `{ state: 'pending' }` (or a distinct 'conflict' state) on key mismatch so only the owning decision drives legs and sets the final status; derive finalStatus from the stored payout row's kind rather than the caller's plan.

findings.title: Action log re-keys all 200 rows on every new entry
findings.description: MatchRail renders `entries.slice(-200).map((line, i) => <div key={i}>)`. Once the log exceeds 200 lines, each new entry shifts every index by one, so React re-renders and re-styles all 200 rows (colorFor regex x4 per row) on every move instead of appending one. The log tab is open by default on desktop, so this cost lands on every state update of a long game.
findings.fix: Key by the absolute index (`entries.length - 200 + i` clamped at 0) or have the game push `{ id, text }` entries; memoize colorFor per line.

findings.title: Lobby polls three endpoints every 5 s even when the tab is hidden
findings.description: refresh() fans out to getLobby, getInvites and listProfilesApi, and the interval never checks document.hidden or backs off. A player who parks the lobby in a background tab generates 2,160 requests per hour against a gateway that already rate-limits other routes. useRankedQueue (7718) and useGlobalChat (121) both implement visibility back-off, so this is an inconsistency, not a policy.
findings.evidence: useEffect(() => { void refresh(); const t = setInterval(() => { void refresh(); }, 5000); return () => clearInterval(t); }, [refresh]);
findings.fix: Skip the tick while document.hidden (and refresh immediately on visibilitychange), or reuse the self-scheduling setTimeout pattern from useRankedQueue with a 30 s hidden interval.

findings.title: 10-second mulligan deadline lets the opponent force-keep a slow-loading player
findings.description: MULLIGAN_TIMEOUT_MS is 10s and the clock starts in phases.mulligan.onBegin on the master, before either client has necessarily rendered the hand (socket reconnect, art loading, mobile). forceKeepOpponent has no playerID or fairness check, so the opponent can lock in a 7-card hand you never saw, and in solo play the bot's instant keep plus any UI delay makes this reachable too. The per-turn timeout is 90s with a 60s client auto-pass for exactly this reason; the mulligan has no such margin.
findings.fix: Raise the window (30-45s) and/or start the deadline when the first keep/mulligan arrives from either player, so it measures opponent idleness rather than page load.

findings.title: Collection refresh leaves `loading: true` on a 401 that did not clear the session
findings.description: `refreshCollection()` and `syncCollection()` return early on `err.isAuthError`, assuming `onSessionChange` will reset state. But `http.ts:269` throws a plain 401 `ApiError` *without* clearing the session when the replay after a successful refresh is still rejected, so no session event fires and the store stays `loading: true` with the spinner on until the next focus-triggered refresh (throttled to 30s) or sign-in. `syncCollection` has the same pattern at line 513.
findings.fix: Only short-circuit on `SessionExpiredError`; for any other 401 commit a non-loading state with an error message.

findings.title: setTimeouts is unbounded and reclaim reads the live global, so the owner can lock stakes forever
findings.description: setTimeouts only requires non-zero values and reclaim() computes the deadline from the current fundingTimeout/settleTimeout rather than a per-match snapshot. The owner can wait until a high-value match is Funded, set settleTimeout to type(uint64).max, and reclaim then reverts (uint256(fundedAt)+settleTimeout is far in the future), while settle/cancel remain operator-only. The header's guarantee that stakes are never locked if the operator disappears is void. This is audit H-10 and is still present.
findings.fix: Cap both timeouts (e.g. funding <= 24h, settle <= 7d) and store fundingDeadline/settleDeadline in the Match struct at createMatch/deposit time so later admin changes cannot affect open matches.

findings.title: Legacy pool uses ssl rejectUnauthorized:false; render.yaml forces it with PGSSL=1
findings.description: TLS to Supabase/Render Postgres is established without certificate verification whenever the URL mentions render.com/supabase or PGSSL=1 (which render.yaml sets), so a network-position attacker can MITM the database connection carrying wager rows and booster tickets. new-backend distinguishes 'require' (verify) from 'no-verify'; the legacy server only has the insecure mode.
findings.fix: Use `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: <provider CA> }` or `sslmode=verify-full` in the URL; Supabase publishes its CA bundle.

findings.title: PrivyBoundary swallows the SDK crash with no log
findings.description: `componentDidCatch` is an empty body, so whatever made the Privy subtree throw (bad app id, SDK version mismatch, a React hook error) is discarded; the player sees 'unavailable right now' and the developer has nothing in the console. Elsewhere the file goes to lengths to `logPrivyFailure` for a misconfigured origin, but the most severe failure mode is silent.
findings.fix: `componentDidCatch(error, info) { console.error('[privy] boundary', error, info.componentStack); }` (gated to non-production if noise is a concern).

findings.title: Rake is read from the live rakeBps at settle, not snapshotted at createMatch
findings.description: settle() computes rake from the mutable rakeBps. The owner can watch for a large Funded match, call setRake(2000, ...) immediately before the operator's settle, and restore it afterwards, taking up to 20% of that specific pot instead of the 10% players agreed to. Players have no way to verify the rake they will pay at deposit time. Audit medium finding, unchanged.
findings.fix: Add uint16 rakeBps to the Match struct, copy it in createMatch, and use m.rakeBps in settle so setRake only affects matches created afterwards.

findings.title: Hand cards keyed by index: drag/hover state sticks to the wrong card after a play
findings.description: The desktop fan (1313), the mobile strip (1387), MobileHandSheet (2808) and MulliganModal (2929) all key hand cards by array index. When card i is played, every card after it shifts left and React reuses the DOM nodes and component state: a DraggableCard mid-drag or a CardHover with a pending long-press timer now belongs to a different card, the `.brd-fan` CSS transition animates the neighbour sliding into the old slot instead of the fan reflowing, and `selectedHand` (also an index) can point at a new card if the server reorders the hand (mulligan redraw).
findings.evidence:
{me.hand.map((id, i) => {
              ...
              return (
                <div key={i} className="brd-fan" style={{
                  ...({ '--rest': rest, '--z': selectedHand === i ? 20 : i } as Vars),
  ...
              : me.hand.map((id, i) => (
                <div key={i} style={{ flex: '0 0 auto' }}>
  ...
          {hand.map((defId, i) => (
            <CardFace key={i} defId={defId} />
findings.fix: Give hand entries a stable id in G (e.g. a per-card uid assigned at draw) or key by `${id}-${occurrence}` computed per render; make `selectedHand` hold that uid instead of an index.

findings.title: One EOA is deployer, owner, operator and feeRecipient; MasterToken.mint is uncapped
findings.description: deployment.json records the same address 0x793a…7E60 as deployer (Ownable owner of all three contracts), WagerEscrow operator and feeRecipient. That key can settle any match to either player (settle only checks winner is p1 or p2, with no proof of result), change rake/timeouts, drain CardPack ETH via withdraw, and mint unlimited MASTER via MasterToken.mint. A single leaked env var equals every escrowed stake plus unlimited token supply. Audit H-4, unchanged in code and in the recorded deployment.
findings.fix: Transfer ownership of all three contracts to a multisig/timelock, run the operator on a separate low-privilege hot key, point feeRecipient at a treasury, and either cap MasterToken supply or renounce mint after distribution.

findings.title: src/server.ts, src/db.ts and api/*.ts are never typechecked by the build
findings.description: tsconfig.json includes only `src` and explicitly excludes src/server.ts and src/db.ts; api/ has no tsconfig and is outside `include`, so `tsc -b` (the first half of `npm run build`) skips the Koa server, the Postgres layer and both Vercel functions. They run through tsx/esbuild which strips types without checking. A scratchpad tsconfig that includes those four files currently reports 0 errors, so this is an enforcement gap today rather than a live break, but any future type error there ships silently.
findings.evidence:
$ sed -n 20,24p tsconfig.json
    "types": ["node", "vite/client"]
  },
  "include": ["src"],
  "exclude": ["src/server.ts", "src/db.ts"]
$ ls api/tsconfig.json
ls: cannot access 'api/tsconfig.json': No such file or directory
$ npx tsc -p <scratchpad tsconfig including src/server.ts src/db.ts api/*.ts> | grep -c 'error TS'
0
findings.fix: Add a `tsconfig.server.json` (types: node only) covering src/server*.ts, src/db.ts and api/*.ts, and run it from `npm run build`/CI alongside the browser project via `tsc -b` references.

findings.title: `/gw/:path*` rewrite is dead config; SPA fallback regex drops any dotted path
findings.description: No code references `/gw`: the only mention is a comment in src/api/config.ts, and API_BASE resolves straight to https://api.ocva.online. The rewrite therefore proxies nothing but still advertises a cross-origin passthrough. The SPA fallback `/((?!.*\.).*)` rewrites only paths without a dot; the app uses hash routing (`#match=`) so this is harmless today, but a future path such as /u/name.eth would 404 instead of loading the app.
findings.evidence:
$ sed -n 6,9p vercel.json
  "rewrites": [
    { "source": "/gw/:path*", "destination": "https://api.ocva.online/:path*" },
    { "source": "/((?!.*\\.).*)", "destination": "/index.html" }
$ grep -rn '/gw' src api index.html
src/api/config.ts:87: * proxy path (e.g. `/gw` — see vercel.json): Vercel rewrites do not carry
$ sed -n 6478p src/App.tsx
  const inviteUrl = window.location.origin + window.location.pathname + '#match=' + seat.matchID;
findings.fix: Remove the `/gw` rewrite (or start using it so the gateway CORS allowlist is no longer needed), and replace the regex fallback with `{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/index.html" }` relying on Vercel's filesystem-first handling.

findings.title: Fabricated 'minted' offset also eats real sellable supply
findings.description: `BOOSTER_MINTED_OFFSET = 37` is documented as a display-only marketing number added to the real mint count. In `server.ts:354` and `:379` the sold-out check is `supply + BOOSTER_MINTED_OFFSET >= BOOSTER_SUPPLY_CAP`, so with the default cap of 100 only 63 tickets can ever be sold, and the count shown to buyers is inflated. The header comment also says the default cap is 2000 while the code says 100, and `BOOSTER_PRICE_SOL` is described as 'denominated in ETH' while charged as lamports.
findings.fix: Remove the offset from the sold-out gate (or remove the offset entirely; showing a fake mint count to buyers is a trust problem) and fix the stale comments.

findings.title: Solana connectors are dead UI code but ship @solana/web3.js in the main bundle
findings.description: `connectSolana`, `connectSolanaWith`, `getSolanaWallet`, `getPhantom`, `detectSolanaWallets` and the Wallet-Standard adapter are not called from App.tsx, Settings.tsx or Boosters.tsx (grep finds no UI call sites), and `auth.signMessageSolana` is likewise unused. The game signs in only on Robinhood Chain. Yet `wallet.ts` is eagerly imported by App.tsx and imports `PublicKey, Transaction, VersionedTransaction` from `@solana/web3.js`, pulling several hundred KB (plus the Buffer polyfill) into first paint. The module also registers `wallet-standard` window listeners at import time.
findings.fix: Move the Solana connectors to a separate lazily-imported module (or delete them), and keep `wallet.ts` free of `@solana/web3.js` so the EVM-only path has no Solana weight.

findings.title: SECURITY_AUDIT.pdf predates 51 commits incl. Privy auth, Vercel pg functions, EVM packs
findings.description: The audit PDF was committed 2026-07-27 in the same commit that introduced new-backend. Since then 51 commits have landed, adding Privy login, two Postgres-backed Vercel functions (api/chat.ts, api/presence.ts), EVM booster-pack minting (src/pack-evm.ts, scripts/evm-deploy*.mjs), masterquest and the Sproto faction rework. Keeping a 3-month-old audit at the repo root without a scope/date note implies coverage the document cannot have.
findings.evidence:
$ git log -1 --format='%ci %h' -- SECURITY_AUDIT.pdf
2026-07-27 19:49:22 +0300 62834ca
$ git log --diff-filter=A --format=%ci -- new-backend/package.json | tail -1
2026-07-27 19:49:22 +0300
$ git rev-list --count 62834ca..HEAD
51
$ ls -la api
chat.ts (Oct 28)  presence.ts (Oct 24)
findings.fix: Move the PDF to docs/security/2026-07-27-audit.pdf with a SECURITY.md stating its commit hash and scope, and list what has changed since so a follow-up review can be scoped.

findings.title: master_wager has no draw/expire path: an Active match with no winner locks both stakes forever
findings.description: settle_match requires a winner that is creator or opponent, and cancel_match only works from Open state by the creator after the timeout. A draw, a permanent disconnect, an oracle outage, or a winner whose ATA cannot receive (frozen/closed) leaves the match in Active with 2x wager in the vault and no instruction that can ever move it. server-wager.ts explicitly returns on draw with 'no settle path yet' and DEPLOY.md lists this as an open issue. The oracle also cannot be rotated to rescue it because there is no admin recovery instruction.
findings.fix: Add an oracle-signed settle_draw (refund both, no burn) and a permissionless expire_match that refunds both after created_at + a settle timeout, mirroring WagerEscrow.reclaim.

findings.title: Presence function runs CREATE TABLE/INDEX on every cold start request
findings.description: ensureTable issues DDL from the request path on every cold Vercel instance; with many concurrent cold starts this means many concurrent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements against Neon (which can raise 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint pg_type_typname_nsp_index' under contention) and adds latency to the first heartbeat. api/chat.ts, by contrast, assumes its table exists, so the two functions follow different schema-management rules.
findings.fix: Create the table once via a migration/SQL script in the Neon project and drop ensureTable.

findings.title: `useOnlineCount` is mounted twice, doubling the 30s poll to a Postgres-backed function
findings.description: `useOnlineCount()` starts its own `setInterval(read, 30_000)` per mounting component; App.tsx mounts it at lines 2060 and 4952, so every open tab issues two GETs per 30s plus the heartbeat POST, each of which runs a `count(*)` on `player_presence` in a Vercel function. With N players that is 3N requests/30s for one number. No `AbortController` is attached, so an unmounted component's in-flight fetch is only guarded by the `alive` flag.
findings.fix: Lift the count into a module-level store (like `collection.ts`) with one poller shared by all subscribers, and have the heartbeat POST's response feed the same store so signed-in clients need no separate GET.

findings.title: settleCustodialMatch is check-then-act with no lock: concurrent calls double-pay
findings.description: Settlement reads the row, checks settle_sig/refunded in JS, builds and broadcasts an SPL transfer, and only then writes settle_sig. Two /api/result posts arriving within the ~2-10s confirmation window (both players' clients post on game end, or an attacker posts twice) both see settle_sig = NULL and both send a payout, draining 2x the pot from the shared escrow wallet. The comment claims idempotency but nothing enforces it.
findings.fix: Claim the settlement first with an atomic `UPDATE custodial_wagers SET settling = TRUE WHERE match_id = $1 AND settle_sig IS NULL AND NOT refunded AND NOT settling RETURNING *` (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction) and only broadcast when the claim returned a row; persist the tx hash before broadcasting.

findings.title: CardPack pull is readable before _safeMint, so a contract minter can revert bad packs for free
findings.description: cardOf[id] is written at line 58 and the pseudo-random seed (prevrandao, timestamp, sender, nonce) is fully known to the caller, then _safeMint at line 61 calls onERC721Received on a contract buyer. A minter contract can read cardOf(tokenId) inside the hook and revert unless the pull is a chase card, unwinding the whole mintPack and recovering the ETH; nonReentrant does not help because nothing re-enters. A cheaper variant is to eth_call mintPack against the pending block and only broadcast on a good result. This is audit finding H-8 and it is unchanged in the current source.
findings.fix: Move to a two-step commit/reveal (pay now, reveal from a later blockhash in a separate tx, with a deadline) or a VRF, and at minimum require msg.sender == tx.origin / use _mint instead of _safeMint so a receiver hook cannot veto the pull.

findings.title: Copy-feedback timeouts are never cleared; setState fires after unmount
findings.description: flashCopied (MatchSeat 6480), copyAddr (Landing 2130, ProfilePage 2914), TokenAnnouncement.copy (2686), Boosters copyAddr/PendingHash (226, 779), Settings copyWallet/flash (519, 562) and Board.flash (847) all schedule a bare setTimeout that calls setState 1.5-2.2 s later with no cleanup. Pressing copy and immediately navigating (MatchSeat unmounts when the opponent joins ~1.7 s later, which is exactly this window) runs setState on an unmounted component. React 18 no longer warns, but the pattern also means a fast double-click leaves two timers racing the same state.
findings.evidence:
const [copied, setCopied] = useState<'' | 'link' | 'id'>('');
  const flashCopied = (which: 'link' | 'id') => { setCopied(which); setTimeout(() => setCopied(''), 1600); };
findings.fix: Add a tiny `useFlash(ms)` hook that stores the timer in a ref, clears it on re-trigger and on unmount, and use it at all nine sites.

findings.title: CardPack keeps overpayment, has no supply cap, and withdraw(to) accepts address(0)
findings.description: mintPack requires msg.value >= packPrice and never refunds the excess, so any wallet that pads value (or the client's cached PACK_PRICE_ETH fallback when the owner has lowered the price) silently overpays. nextId is unbounded so the advertised scarcity is not enforced on-chain. withdraw(address to) has no zero-address check; a single bad argument burns the whole balance. All three are the audit's CardPack medium items and remain.
findings.fix: Require msg.value == packPrice (or refund the delta), add a maxPacks/maxSupply check against nextId, and require(to != address(0)) in withdraw.

findings.title: Dependency bloat: server/native packages in the SPA's deps, bs58 undeclared
findings.description: `bufferutil` and `utf-8-validate` are listed as hard dependencies although nothing imports them and vite.config.ts externalizes them; they are optional ws accelerators and pull native prebuilds on every install. `koa-static` exists only for the legacy src/server.ts. Conversely scripts/attach-sprotos-to-collection.mts and scripts/mint-sprotos.mts import `bs58`, which is not declared and resolves only as a transitive dependency of @solana/web3.js, so a lockfile bump can break them. The .npmrc `legacy-peer-deps=true` hides all peer conflicts repo-wide to tolerate drei@10 on react@18.

$ grep -c . <(grep -rlE "from ['\"](bufferutil|utf-8-validate)" src api scripts)
0
$ grep -n 'external' vite.config.ts
      external: ['bufferutil', 'utf-8-validate'],
$ grep -hoE "from '[^.][^']+'" scripts/*.mts | sort -u | grep bs58
from 'bs58'
$ grep -n '"bs58"' package.json || echo 'bs58 NOT in package.json'
bs58 NOT in package.json
$ cat .npmrc | tail -1
legacy-peer-deps=true
findings.fix: Drop bufferutil/utf-8-validate (or move them to optionalDependencies), declare bs58 explicitly, and move koa-static plus the Koa server scripts out once render.yaml is retired.

findings.title: Anchor and deploy scripts default to mainnet with real keys; `anchor test` would hit mainnet
findings.description: Anchor.toml sets provider.cluster = "mainnet" with the default ~/.config/solana/id.json wallet, so `anchor test`, `anchor deploy` and `anchor migrate` run against mainnet-beta unless overridden. initialize.ts defaults SOLANA_RPC to api.mainnet-beta.solana.com and signs with the same wallet, and scripts/evm-deploy.mjs defaults ROBINHOOD_RPC to the Robinhood mainnet endpoint and broadcasts two deployments with no dry-run flag or confirmation. A copy-paste of the README commands spends real SOL/ETH by default.
findings.fix: Default Anchor.toml to localnet (override cluster via `anchor deploy --provider.cluster mainnet`), default script RPCs to devnet/testnet, and require an explicit `--mainnet` or CONFIRM_MAINNET=1 env before broadcasting.

findings.title: No per-turn combat flag: multiple combat phases per turn and zero-attacker combats
findings.description: confirmAttackers does not record that combat has happened, and after confirmBlocks the attacker is returned to Stage.NULL with the full move list. A player can attack with meme A, see the block and its result, then declare and confirm meme B as a second combat, repeating once per untapped meme; this leaks block information and breaks the one-combat-per-turn model that the bot and Board assume. confirmAttackers is also callable directly with zero attackers (verified: activePlayers became {attacker:'afk', defender:'blockers'}), forcing the defender to click through an empty combat and resetting nothing.
findings.fix: Add `G.combat.declaredThisTurn` (reset in turn.onBegin); reject confirmAttackers/goToCombat when it is set or when attackers is empty, and set it when combat is confirmed.

findings.title: First result sweep after boot re-reads every finished match ever stored
findings.description: cursor starts at 0, so the first pass lists all gameover matches in the bgio store and calls recordFinishedMatch for each, which does a store.fetch(state+metadata) and a locking transaction per match that returns 'duplicate'. As the Games table grows to tens of thousands of rows, each restart (every deploy) costs a long burst of Postgres reads and row locks on game.matches before the sweeper becomes current.
findings.fix: Seed the cursor from `MAX(finished_at)` in game.match_results (minus the overlap) on boot, or filter the candidate list with a NOT EXISTS against match_results before fetching state.

findings.title: block.prevrandao is a constant on Arbitrum Orbit chains, collapsing the entropy further
findings.description: foundry.toml describes Robinhood Chain as an Arbitrum Orbit L2. On Arbitrum Nitro-based chains block.prevrandao (and block.difficulty) returns a fixed constant rather than beacon randomness, and block.timestamp is sequencer-assigned and often identical across consecutive L2 blocks. The seed in _rand therefore reduces to (constant, coarse timestamp, msg.sender, nonce, salt), all of which a buyer can enumerate off-chain before sending, so the pack contents are computable in advance even without the revert trick in contracts-01.
findings.fix: Do not source randomness from block fields on this chain at all; use commit/reveal keyed on a future blockhash supplied by the sequencer, or an off-chain VRF/oracle signature verified on-chain.

findings.title: `connectRobinhoodChain` returns a checksummed address while `connectEvm` lowercases
findings.description: `connectEvm()` lowercases the account (line 181) and `Session.address` is documented as 'Lowercased for EVM', but `connectRobinhoodChain()` (the one actually used for sign-in and for linking in Settings.tsx:594) returns the raw EIP-55 string. The link flow sends the mixed-case address to `/auth/addresses/nonce`, and anything keyed on the client by that string (cache keys, `sameAddress` comparisons) relies on ad-hoc `.toLowerCase()` calls scattered through `collection.ts` and `linked-wallets.ts`.
findings.fix: Normalise to lowercase in `connectRobinhoodChain()` (or return both forms) so one convention holds everywhere.

findings.title: Permissionless reclaim lets a loser front-run settle after settleTimeout and convert a loss to a refund
findings.description: Once fundedAt + settleTimeout (default 1 day) has passed, both settle (operator) and reclaim (anyone) are valid on the same Funded match. A player who knows they lost a long match can submit reclaim ahead of the operator's settle; _refund flips status to Cancelled and the operator's settle then reverts with 'not funded'. The timeout exists for operator failure, but it also hands the loser a griefing/escape hatch whenever settlement is slow. Audit medium, unchanged.
findings.fix: Give the operator a grace window that is exclusive (e.g. reclaim only after settleTimeout + grace, or let the operator extend fundedAt by posting a 'match started' heartbeat), and make settle emit a result hash players can dispute instead of racing.

findings.title: On-chain card index space is Object.values(CARDS) order with no frozen manifest or test
findings.description: Both the metadata generator and the client decoder define card index N as the Nth non-node entry of Object.values(CARDS). Any insert, reorder or deletion in src/cards.ts silently remaps every already-minted token on the live CardPack (0x5720…30b3, cardCount 80) to a different card, and the on-chain tokenURI (baseURI + index + '.json') would then serve the wrong art. Nothing pins this ordering and no test compares it against public/nft/index.json. Audit L-6, unchanged.
findings.fix: Commit public/nft/index.json as the canonical index->cardId manifest, have pack-evm.ts and the backend cardIndex read it, and add a test asserting the live catalogue still matches the committed manifest for indices 0..cardCount-1.

findings.title: Postgres init failure silently falls back to in-memory store in production
findings.description: If the DATABASE_URL connection or any boot DDL fails, initDb logs and sets pool = null, and every store function then uses process-local Maps. Booster payment-signature dedupe, ticket rows, challenge state and ranked results then live only in RAM: a restart lets a payment signature be replayed to mint again, sold tickets vanish, and the custodial path throws 'Postgres not initialized' on every call. On Render's free plan the instance sleeps and restarts regularly, so this would be hit in practice.
findings.fix: Fail the process when DATABASE_URL is set but unreachable (exit non-zero so the platform restarts it), and keep the in-memory path strictly for DATABASE_URL-unset local dev.

findings.title: Master-mute logic copied five times; Boosters' copy breaks per-track mute
findings.description: Landing (App 2091), ProfilePage (2896), RulebookPage (1636), SettingsPage (Settings 533) and BoostersPage each blanket-assign `.muted` to every <audio>, and BgMusic documents that it relies on a PREFS_EVENT dispatch afterwards to re-assert a track the player muted individually. Boosters' copy omits that dispatch, so a player who muted only the menu music and then toggles the Boosters mute off ends up with the menu track un-muted. Five hand-rolled copies of the same side effect is exactly how this drift happened.
findings.fix: Create one `useMasterMute()` hook (read/write 'ocva.muted', apply to media, dispatch PREFS_EVENT) in a shared module and use it from all five screens.

findings.title: deposit writes state after the external transfer and settle/cancel/reclaim lack nonReentrant
findings.description: deposit() calls token.safeTransferFrom before setting m.amt1/m.amt2, and settle, settleDraw, cancelMatch and reclaim are not guarded. With a hook-bearing token (ERC-777 style or any token that calls back), a re-entrant reclaim during the second deposit could credit a refund and then deposit resumes and marks the match Funded, leaving the contract owing more than it holds. Not exploitable against the deployed plain OZ MasterToken, but the token is constructor-set and the contract is generic. Audit H-11, unchanged.
findings.fix: Add nonReentrant to settle, settleDraw, cancelMatch and reclaim (cheap, no behaviour change), and document that only non-hook ERC-20s are supported.

findings.title: PublicProfile renders a 'custom deck' section that can never have data
findings.description: The loader explicitly setDeck([]) (the comment explains other players' decks are not readable), yet the component keeps `deck` state, a deckGrouped useMemo, validateDeck(deck) on every render, and ~50 lines of grid markup for a deck list that is always empty, so every public profile shows "X'S CUSTOM DECK (0/60)" and "This player hasn't published a custom deck yet." The phrase is also misleading: there is no publishing feature.
findings.fix: Remove the deck state, deckGrouped, deckValid and the deck card from PublicProfile (or replace it with the ranked standing / recent matches the API does expose).

findings.title: Board requests profiles for fallback and bot names on every match
findings.description: refreshProfiles fetches GET /api/profiles/<name> for both seats using whatever myName/oppName resolved to. In solo play oppName is 'Bot (normal)' or a Masterquest rival title like 'X — Y', and before matchData arrives it can be 'Player 0'. Each is a guaranteed 404 fired on mount and again 2 s after gameover, which is wasted bandwidth, log noise on the gateway, and a reason the profile route gets rate-limited for a real player.
findings.fix: Skip the fetch when isSolo, when the name is the `Player N` fallback, or when matchData has not supplied a name yet; add an alive guard to the .then calls.

findings.title: Defender lifelink can heal twice; aura_lifelink/mill3/discardRandom are implemented but no card uses them
findings.description: In the blocked branch the defender gains bPower inside the loop when the blocker carries aura_lifelink, and then applyLifelink(G, defPid, totalDealtByBlockers) heals again if they also own a lifelink_all machine (Treasury), so the same damage heals twice. Today this is latent because no card in cards.ts has effect 'aura_lifelink' (verified: effects used by the catalogue exclude aura_lifelink, mill3 and discardRandom). Those three effect ids, the `PlayerView` import, `totalGas()`, and PlayerState.hasDrawnForTurn (written in setup, never read) are dead code that still costs review and bot-enumeration time; derivePrimaryColor's comment also claims a 'sol' fallback while the code returns 'bnb' for an empty deck.
findings.fix: Route all lifelink through applyLifelink (machine OR aura, once), delete the `&& false` branch, drop the unused import/fields/effects or add cards that use them, and fix the derivePrimaryColor doc.

findings.title: Payout tx hash is persisted only after confirmation; a timeout leaves it unrecorded
findings.description: sendAndConfirmTransaction can throw after the transaction was broadcast (blockhash expiry / confirmation timeout / RPC rotation mid-call). The catch only logs, settle_sig stays NULL, and the next /api/result for the match sends a second payout. The same pattern applies to the draw refund and adminRefund paths. There is no record of the signed transaction before broadcast, so an operator cannot even tell whether funds moved.
findings.fix: Sign the transaction, persist its signature and raw bytes to the row, then broadcast and reconcile by signature on retry (the sign/persist/broadcast/reconcile pattern in new-backend/services/wager/src/services/payoutRunner.ts).

findings.title: Compromised Alchemy key removed from code but rotation is only a note; no proof it happened
findings.description: Audit H-5 flagged a live Alchemy key in nine files. The current tree has removed it (public keyless RPC everywhere, src/wager-evm*.ts deleted) and deployment.json carries a note that the key 'is compromised and must be rotated'. The key remains in git history, and nothing in the repo records that rotation occurred, so the residual risk (quota abuse billed to the project) is open until the dashboard rotation is confirmed.
findings.evidence: "rpcNote": "Public keyless endpoint. A live Alchemy key was committed here; it is compromised and must be rotated. Never commit a provider key."
findings.fix: Rotate/delete the key in the Alchemy dashboard, record the date in SECURITY.md or the commit, and consider rewriting history or treating the old key as burned.

findings.title: Unreferenced LFS video and 12 MB of uncompressed MP3 in public/
findings.description: public/intro.mp4 (2.1 MB, LFS) is referenced by nothing in src or index.html — only rules-intro.mp4 is used. login-theme.mp3 is 8.0 MB and battle-music.mp3 4.3 MB; together the four MP3s are over 12 MB served to every player who reaches the login screen. There are also 107 PNGs vs 94 WebPs in public/, with the five largest non-card PNGs (masterquest-map, egregore-bg, wizard-battle-bg, sproto-gremlin, intro) at 2.9-3.5 MB each still shipped as PNG.

$ grep -rn '"/intro.mp4\|/intro\.mp4' src index.html | wc -l

$ find public -type f -printf '%s %p\n' | sort -rn | head -6 | awk '{printf "%.1fMB %s\n", $1/1048576, $2}'
172.1MB public/rules-intro.mp4
8.0MB public/login-theme.mp3
4.3MB public/battle-music.mp3

3.4MB public/egregore-bg.png

$ find public -type f | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3

findings.fix: Delete intro.mp4, re-encode the MP3s at ~96 kbps (or OGG/Opus) and convert the large backdrop PNGs to WebP/AVIF; add a `scripts/optimize-assets.mjs` so new drops go through the same pipeline.

findings.title: Match and vault accounts are never closed; rent is leaked on every match
findings.description: settle_match and cancel_match set state to Settled/Cancelled but neither closes match_account nor the vault token account, so the creator's rent (Match 8+211 bytes plus a 165-byte token account, roughly 0.0036 SOL) is permanently stranded per match and the vault stays open with authority = match PDA. There is no close instruction, so even the admin cannot reclaim it.
findings.fix: Add `close = creator` to match_account in CancelMatch and a close_match instruction (or close in settle) that CPI-closes the empty vault via token::close_account with the PDA signer and returns lamports to the creator.

findings.title: Custodial deposit signature can be reused across matches (no global uniqueness)
findings.description: `markFunded` verifies that the transaction transfers `>= expectedAmount` from the player's ATA to the escrow ATA, but the memo that binds a deposit to `mm:<matchID>:<playerID>` is only *warned* about when missing, and the idempotency check compares the signature only to the same seat of the same row. One real deposit signature can therefore be submitted as funding for seat 0 of match A and again for match B (or the other seat, if both are the same amount), making two matches 'funded' with one stake; the settle path then pays out from the hot wallet twice. This is on the legacy Koa server (`server.ts:548` dynamic-imports it), so exposure depends on whether that server is still deployed with `CUSTODIAL_ESCROW_KEYPAIR` set.
findings.fix: Require the memo to match (fail, not warn) and add a `UNIQUE` index on the deposit signature across all rows (`custodial_deposits(sig) UNIQUE`), rejecting any signature already bound to another match/seat.

findings.title: Menu music restarts when opening a player profile from the lobby
findings.description: showMusic lists eight views but not 'view-profile', so <MenuMusic /> unmounts when the player taps a name in the lobby leaderboard and remounts (from 0:00, after a fresh autoplay attempt that may be blocked) when they go back. The comment above says the audio element is shared precisely so the track keeps playing between screens.
findings.fix: Invert the condition (`const showMusic = !seat && !soloCfg`) or add 'view-profile' to the list; better, keep <MenuMusic /> mounted once at the root and let BattleMusic pause it.

findings.title: Legacy server echoes raw error messages (pg, RPC, stack text) to clients
findings.description: The catch-all returns `String(e?.message)` for any thrown error, and several routes do the same (lines 268, 295, 311, 361, 391, 511, 528, 542, 557). pg errors include table/column names and constraint names, and the custodial path returns RPC error text with URLs. This leaks schema and infrastructure detail to unauthenticated callers.
findings.fix: Map known error classes to fixed client-safe messages and log the original server-side (new-backend/packages/shared/src/errors.ts already does this).

findings.title: 91 unreferenced legacy card PNG/JPGs (172 MB) are tracked in git and shipped
findings.description: Every card art path in src/cards.ts now points at public/cards/<faction>/*.webp. The 82 PNG + 9 JPG files sitting directly in public/cards/ (about 2.8 MB each) are referenced by nothing in src or index.html, yet all 91 are tracked in git and copied into dist/ on every build. They make the pack 317 MB, every clone and Vercel build fetch 172 MB of dead art, and dist/ 430 MB.
findings.evidence:
$ for f in public/cards/*.png public/cards/*.jpg; do b=$(basename $f); grep -rq "/cards/$b" src index.html || ...; done
91 unreferenced files, 172 MB
$ grep -oE '/cards/[a-z_0-9-]+\.(png|jpg)' src/cards.ts | sort -u | wc -l
0
$ git ls-files public/cards/*.png public/cards/*.jpg | wc -l
91
$ git count-objects -vH | grep size-pack
size-pack: 317.63 MiB
$ du -sh public dist
422M public
430M dist
findings.fix: Delete the root-level public/cards/*.png|jpg (and the other unreferenced PNGs like intro.png / egregore-bg.png if superseded) in a single commit; consider `git lfs migrate` or a history rewrite later if clone size matters.

findings.title: `masterUi` converts UI amounts with float math
findings.description: `masterUi(n)` computes `BigInt(Math.floor(n * 10 ** 6))`. Binary floating point makes e.g. `1.15 * 1e6 === 1149999.9999999998`, which floors to `1149999`, so a 1.15 $MASTER wager is recorded as 1.149999 and the deposit check in `server-custodial.ts:979` (`amt >= expectedAmount`) and payouts drift by base units. `server-custodial.createIntent` feeds user-entered numbers straight into it.
findings.fix: Parse the decimal string instead (split on '.', pad the fraction to 6 digits, build the BigInt), as `api/wager.ts formatAmount` already does in the other direction.

findings.title: Deposit signature is replayable across seats and matches; memo is only a warning
findings.description: markFunded stores the deposit signature in a per-seat column and the only replay check is `already === args.signature` for the same seat of the same match. The memo binding the deposit to (matchID, playerID) is logged but not enforced. One real deposit therefore funds seat 0 and seat 1 of the same match (same pubkey), or seat N of any number of other matches with the same amount. With both seats 'funded' from one stake, /api/result (server-01) pays 1.8x the single deposit, and a draw refunds two stakes for one.
findings.fix: Make the deposit signature a globally unique primary key in its own deposits table (as new-backend's wager.deposits does), reject when the memo does not match, and require the two seats to be funded by different pubkeys.

findings.title: No tests for the refresh single-flight, 401 replay or 429 budget
findings.description: `http.ts` is the most security-sensitive client module (one refresh in flight, never loop, family revocation on reuse) and exports `isRefreshing()` explicitly as a "test seam", yet no test file imports `http.ts` or `session.ts` (grep over `src/**/*.test.ts` finds none). The concurrent-401 dedup, the `tokenUsed !== currentToken` replay-without-refresh branch, the no-session `SessionExpiredError` path and the 429 budget are all untested; a regression here logs every user out.
findings.fix: Add `src/api/http.test.ts` with a stubbed `fetch`: ten parallel 401s produce exactly one `/auth/refresh`; a failed refresh clears the session and throws `SessionExpiredError`; POST is not retried on 429; `Retry-After` is honoured.

findings.title: Legacy POST /api/result lets any client name the winner and trigger escrow payout
findings.description: The legacy Koa server's /api/result route has no authentication and takes matchID, winner, loser, draw and wager.winnerSeat straight from the request body, then calls settleCustodialMatch with the client-supplied seat. Anyone with curl who knows a funded matchID can pay themselves 90% of the pot and burn the rest. The same body also drives recordMatch (leaderboard) and RatingService.ingestMatchResult (ranked). This server is NOT what runs at api.ocva.online today (see server-21), but it is still the repo's `npm start` target and render.yaml blueprint.
findings.fix: Delete the route (and src/server-custodial.ts) or derive the outcome exclusively from boardgame.io's server-held ctx.gameover as new-backend's results/recorder.ts does. Never accept a winner from a request.

findings.title: Fixed-position lobby buttons collide with the install banner on phones
findings.description: On mobile the Lobby pins 'VS Bot' at bottom 52px+safe-area and 'Enter Plaza' at bottom 104px (right 12, z 50, ~44px tall). InstallPrompt is also fixed at bottom 12px spanning left 12 to right 12 (z 90, ~60px tall) and WalletLinkPrompt at bottom 16px (z 140). On a 390px-wide phone the install banner covers roughly bottom 12-72px, which overlaps the 'VS Bot' button at 52-96px, and the sticky FooterStatsBar sits under all of them. A first-time iOS Safari visitor (install hint shown) therefore has the solo button partially covered and the footer stats unreadable.
findings.evidence:
<button
          onClick={onSolo}
          title="Play a single-player match against the bot"
          style={{
            position: 'fixed', zIndex: 50,
            ...(mobile
              ? { right: 12, bottom: 'calc(52px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))' }
              : { right: 16, top: 64 }),
  ...
      position: 'fixed', left: 12, right: 12, bottom: 'calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))',
      maxWidth: 460, marginLeft: 'auto', marginRight: 'auto',  // InstallPrompt
findings.fix: Move 'VS Bot' and 'Enter Plaza' into the lobby's center-column tab row (Quick Match already lives there) or into FooterStatsBar, and give the three bottom banners one shared stacking slot (a `<BottomDock>` that renders at most one at a time).

findings.title: Three divergent useIsMobile hooks and per-card matchMedia listeners
findings.description: useIsMobile is implemented in App.tsx (default 720, matchMedia + legacy addListener fallback), Board.tsx (identical copy) and Boosters.tsx (hard-coded 900, no fallback, no initial onChange). Callers additionally pass 767, 860, 920, 1000 and 1279, so 'mobile' means something different on every screen. Because Board's CardFace calls useIsMobile and useIsShort per card, every hand card, mulligan card and Zone card creates two MediaQueryList objects and two listeners.
findings.fix: Move one `useMediaQuery(query)` to src/hooks.ts backed by a module-level cache of MediaQueryList + subscribers (or useSyncExternalStore), define named breakpoints once, and have CardFace take `compact` as a prop from its parent instead of subscribing per card.

findings.title: No legacy REST route is authenticated; body.name / ?name= is the identity
findings.description: Profiles, profile updates (including walletAddress linking), decks, challenges, booster redemption and ranked queue all take the acting player's name from the request. Anyone can overwrite another player's bio/avatar/wallet, delete their decks, accept their challenges, or link a victim's wallet address to an attacker-controlled profile so getProfileByWallet resolves wrong. The comment at line 241 acknowledges it ('Trusted in this single-user-per-name model').
findings.fix: Retire the legacy server in favour of new-backend (JWT from wallet challenge-response, identity only from req.auth). If it must stay, gate every mutating route on a verified session.

findings.title: Booster confirm is check-then-mint: one payment can mint two NFTs
findings.description: /api/boosters/confirm checks isBoosterPaymentSigUsed, then verifies the payment (up to 60s of RPC polling), mints the Metaplex Core NFT, and only then inserts the row whose payment_sig UNIQUE constraint would have caught the duplicate. Two concurrent confirms with the same signature both pass the pre-check and both mint; the second insert fails with 23505 after the NFT already exists, so the buyer receives two tickets for one payment and the second is unrecorded. nextBoosterTicketNumber (MAX+1) has the same race and will also throw on ticket_number UNIQUE after the mint.
findings.fix: Reserve the payment signature first (INSERT a pending row with payment_sig as the key, or a dedicated reservations table) and mint only if the insert succeeded; allocate ticket numbers from a sequence.

findings.title: Deposit check accepts any amount >= stake; overpayment is silently kept
findings.description: The transfer matcher uses `amt >= expectedAmount`, so a player who sends more than the stake is credited for exactly one stake and the excess is never refunded. Combined with server-03, one large transfer can also satisfy expectations of several smaller matches.
findings.evidence:
const amt = BigInt(info.amount ?? info.tokenAmount?.amount ?? 0);
if (matchSrc && matchDst && amt >= expectedAmount) sawTransfer = true;
findings.fix: Require an exact match (`amt === expectedAmount`) as new-backend's verifyDepositTx does, and surface a clear error for the wrong amount.

findings.title: Legacy body reader has no size limit and /api/* answers CORS with '*'
findings.description: readJson concatenates the whole request body into a string with no cap, so a single client can post hundreds of MB and exhaust memory on the free Render instance. The same middleware sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every /api/ response, so any site can call the unauthenticated mutating routes from a victim's browser (though with no cookies there is little to steal beyond the wallet-address linking in server-08).
findings.fix: Use koa-bodyparser with a 256 KB limit (new-backend uses express.json({limit}) plus nginx client_max_body_size) and restrict CORS to the PROD_ORIGINS allow-list already defined at line 35.

findings.title: All three contracts use single-step Ownable; renounce or a typo bricks setOperator and withdraw
findings.description: WagerEscrow, CardPack and MasterToken inherit OZ Ownable rather than Ownable2Step. A mistyped transferOwnership or an accidental renounceOwnership permanently freezes setOperator (if the operator key is lost the escrow can only be drained via the 1-day reclaim path) and CardPack.withdraw (stranding all sale ETH). Audit medium, unchanged.
findings.fix: Switch to Ownable2Step and override renounceOwnership to revert (or require a timelock) on the two contracts that hold funds.

findings.title: ensureSchema runs DDL at request time and caches a rejected promise forever
findings.description: The custodial table is created lazily on the first wager request, and `_schemaReady` is assigned before the promise settles. If that first CREATE TABLE fails (transient DB blip, or getPool() is null because db.ts fell back to memory), every later wager call awaits the same rejected promise until the process restarts, turning a transient error into a permanent outage of the money path.
findings.fix: Create the table in initDb() at boot (or a migration) and reset `_schemaReady = null` in a `.catch` so a failed attempt can be retried.

findings.title: Admin refund token compared with === and no rate limit
findings.description: /api/wager/admin/refund authenticates with a single static header compared using `!==`, which is not constant-time, and there is no rate limiting anywhere on the legacy server, so the token can be brute-forced or timing-probed. A successful guess lets the caller trigger on-chain refunds of any match.
findings.fix: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, add a per-IP limiter, and prefer the operator-role model of new-backend (wallet signature + OPERATOR_ADDRESSES).

findings.title: Server card catalogue is stale: base_moose missing, Knowledge starter deck differs from client
findings.description: The vendored server copy (dated 2026-10-23) has 85 cards; the client has 86. 'base_moose' (Oversized Moose with Socks) exists only on the client. The server's validateDeck therefore rejects any custom deck containing it with 'Unknown card id', so the card is unplayable online, and chooseColor with such a deck returns INVALID_MOVE on the master with no client-visible error (the client does not apply chooseColor optimistically because it uses random). The server's STARTER_DECKS.base also differs: client has base_moose x3 / base_bridge x1 / base_airdrop x0, server has base_moose x0 / base_bridge x2 / base_airdrop x2, so the deck the client previews is not the deck the master shuffles.
findings.fix: Re-run the documented `cp ../../../src/cards.ts src/game/cards.ts` and re-apply the header, and add a CI check (or a shared package) that fails when the two files diverge in anything but the header.

findings.title: Fallback-copy test asserts only that a string came back
findings.description: The test 'an unnamed failure falls through to the generic mapper, not to silence' checks `typeof text === 'string'` and `length > 0`. `linkedWalletErrorText` would pass that even if it returned the raw server prose, the reason slug, or `'[object Object]'`; the behaviour the test name promises (delegation to `errorText`) is not asserted.
findings.fix: Assert `expect(text).toBe(errorText(failure('some_future_reason')))` and that it does not contain the reason slug.

findings.title: Most modals have no dialog role, focus trap, initial focus or Escape handling
findings.description: SoloSetupModal (6845), ProfileEditModal (4567), SavedDeckLibrary, DeckWorkspace's mobile drawer (3871), Board's WinnerShareModal (1830), RulesDrawer (3189), MobileHandSheet (2766), Boosters.ModalShell (1009) and Masterquest.modalShell (406) are plain divs with a backdrop onClick. Keyboard users land nowhere when they open, Tab escapes into the page behind, screen readers are not told a dialog opened, and Escape does nothing. The codebase already has the right pattern in ClearDataDialog/UnlinkWalletDialog (role=dialog, aria-modal, labelledby, Escape) and RuleSearch (autofocus), so this is inconsistency rather than ignorance.
findings.fix: Create one `<Modal onClose labelledBy>` primitive (role=dialog, aria-modal, Escape, focus on open, restore focus on close, simple Tab loop) and route all nine modals through it.

findings.title: No tests exist for Game.ts or bot.ts; every rules bug above is untested
findings.description: The repo has nine test files (cards, collection, match-mode, error-text, linked-wallets, lore, privy, ranked-client) and none exercise a single move. Combat resolution, gas payment/discount, mulligan draw counts, deadline moves, playerView hiding, milling, and the bot's legality are all unverified, which is how engine-01, -02, -06, -09, -10 and -12 shipped. The reducer is trivially drivable headless (InitializeGame + CreateGameReducer from boardgame.io/internal, as used to verify this review), so the cost of a test harness is small.
findings.evidence:
export const ChainsTCG: Game<GState> = {
  name: 'chains-tcg',

  minPlayers: 2,
  maxPlayers: 2,
findings.fix: Add src/Game.test.ts driving the reducer through: opening hands stay at 7, blocked/unblocked combat damage with pumps and auras, canPay/pay with discounts, mulligan floor, forceEndTurn during blockers, playerView hides opponent hand and deck, and a bot-legality fuzz (every enumerateMoves action applies without INVALID_MOVE).

findings.title: Challenge ids come from Math.random and the actor is client-asserted
findings.description: genId builds challenge ids from Math.random plus a timestamp, which is guessable, and updateChallengeStatus only checks that the client-supplied actorName equals the challenge's from/to name. Anyone can enumerate pending challenges via GET /api/challenges/in/<name> and accept or cancel them as either party.
findings.fix: Use crypto.randomUUID() and bind the actor to an authenticated session (new-backend's invites use req.auth.profileId as the WHERE clause).

findings.title: Anyone can pre-create a wager row for any matchID and pin its amount
findings.description: POST /api/wager/intent is unauthenticated and createIntent upserts a custodial_wagers row keyed only by the client-supplied matchID, with first-writer-wins on amount. An attacker who watches the lobby can insert a row for an upcoming match with a tiny or huge amount so the real players' intents fail with 'amount does not match'. playerID is also chosen by the client and never checked against the boardgame.io seat.
findings.fix: Require an authenticated participant of the match (resolve the seat from server-held match metadata) before creating or funding an intent; take the amount from the challenge/match record, not the request.

findings.title: .boost/ is not ignored; bare `frontend`/`backend` patterns ignore any such path
findings.description: .boost/ (the Boost output cache) shows up as untracked in every `git status` and is one careless `git add -A` away from being committed. Separately, .gitignore contains the bare patterns `frontend` and `backend`, which match a file or directory of that name at any depth, so a future src/components/backend.ts or new-backend/packages/frontend would be silently untracked.
findings.evidence:
$ git check-ignore -v .boost || echo NOT IGNORED
NOT IGNORED
$ git status --short | grep boost
?? .boost/
$ sed -n 15,16p .gitignore
frontend
backend
findings.fix: Add `.boost/` to .gitignore and anchor or delete the `frontend`/`backend` lines (`/frontend/`, `/backend/`) if they were for one-off folders.

findings.title: Server log strings use chain-era card names (PEPE, BnB Node) that the client rebrand removed
findings.description: G.log is written by the master using the server's CARDS[...].name, and the client renders that log verbatim. Every one of the 86 shared ids has a different name on the server (e.g. eth_pepe 'PEPE' vs 'Harry Horcrux', node_bnb 'BnB Node' vs 'Spirit Node', sol_wif 'dogwifhat' vs 'Shadow'). Online matches therefore show 'Player 0 summons PEPE.' while the card on the table says Harry Horcrux. cards.test.ts asserts the client has no memecoin names, but the log players actually read comes from the server copy.
findings.evidence:
M('eth_pepe',    'eth', 'PEPE',              5, 5, 6, 'The king of ERC-20 memes.'),
  ...
  X('base_airdrop', 'base', 'Airdrop Szn', 3, 'damageAll_1',  'Points go live. Every Meme on the field takes 1 damage.'),
findings.fix: Re-sync the vendored file (see engine-07). Longer term, log card ids rather than names and let the client resolve display names, so a rename never needs a server deploy.

findings.title: Dev proxy sends /api/chat and /api/presence to the gateway, which has no such routes
findings.description: In production /api/chat and /api/presence are Vercel functions in api/ (pg-backed). In development vite.config.ts proxies every `/api` prefix to api.ocva.online, and neither the gateway code nor INTEGRATION.md mentions presence or chat. findings.title: `useStarterDeck` is a plain async function named like a hook
findings.description: The function adopts a starter deck via three API calls and is invoked from an onClick (`onPick={(color) => { void useStarterDeck(color); }}`). Because its name starts with `use`, eslint-plugin-react-hooks reports 'React Hook useStarterDeck is called in a callback', which either fails lint or trains people to disable the rule that would catch the real violation in frontend-04.
findings.fix: Rename to `adoptStarterDeck`.

findings.title: Anchor client/program use classic SPL Token for MASTER while the custodial path uses Token-2022 for the same mint
findings.description: wager-program.ts derives ATAs with getAssociatedTokenAddress(mint, owner) (default TOKEN_PROGRAM_ID) and passes TOKEN_PROGRAM_ID; lib.rs declares vault/mint/ATAs as anchor_spl::token types and Program<'info, Token>, which Anchor validates as owned by the legacy token program. server-custodial.ts uses TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM_ID for the identical MASTER_MINT and comments that 'pump.fun moved to 2022'. Both cannot be right: if the mint is Token-2022, every master_wager instruction fails account validation and the program can never hold a wager; if it is classic, the custodial ATAs are wrong. DEPLOY.md also tells the operator to verify decimals before deploy, so the mint was never confirmed.
findings.fix: Fetch the mint account owner once (spl-token getMint with programId probing) and hardcode the verified program in one shared constant; if it is Token-2022, port master_wager to anchor_spl::token_interface / InterfaceAccount and pass the matching program id from the client.

findings.title: WagerEscrow and master_wager are deployed/documented but zero real wagers use them
findings.description: All wager settlement in server.ts routes to settleCustodialMatch (server-held Solana hot wallet); the comment states the Anchor path 'has been removed' yet src/server-wager.ts (oracle keypair loader + settle) is still present and dead. Nothing in src/ or new-backend/ imports WagerEscrow or calls createMatch/settle on 0xdbc4…cc3d; new-backend/ROADMAP-ownership.md confirms it 'goes unused'. CardPack is deployed and read by the backend ownership sync, but pack-evm.ts has PACK_MINTING_AVAILABLE = false so the front end does not mint either. The security properties advertised in contracts/README.md (role-gated settlement, pull payments, permissionless reclaim) therefore protect no funds, while the custodial path carries the audit's C-1/C-2 drain risks.
findings.fix: Either wire the EVM client/server to WagerEscrow (createMatch on lobby, deposit from the wallet, settle from the operator key) and retire the custodial hot wallet, or delete server-wager.ts/wager-program.ts/solana/ and mark deployment.json entries as unused so the README stops implying on-chain custody.

findings.title: CARD_PACK read via raw `import.meta.env`, bypassing the sanctioned `readEnv`
findings.description: `config.ts:637-647` declares `readEnv()` the ONLY way to read `VITE_*` values precisely so Vite and Node (vitest/tsx) agree. `pack-evm.ts` reads `import.meta.env.VITE_CARD_PACK` directly with a hardcoded mainnet contract fallback, so tests or scripts importing this module cannot override the pack address via `process.env`, and a second env-reading idiom exists.

  '0x57200fb533b33823f8bd2ac8f3649e3b643830b3') as Address;
findings.fix: Use `readEnv('VITE_CARD_PACK')` and keep the fallback address in one documented constants file.

findings.title: `npm test` is red: root vitest sweeps new-backend/ and 20 files fail to load
findings.description: There is no vitest config and no `test` block in vite.config.ts, so `vitest run` at the repo root collects every *.test.ts including the 26 files under new-backend/services/*/src/__tests__. Those import the workspace package `@chains/shared`, which is only resolvable after `npm ci` inside new-backend/ (new-backend/node_modules does not exist). Result: 20 test files fail at import time on every run, so the suite can never be green and no one can tell a real regression from this noise.

findings.title: Login still carries the whole wallet sign-in path, but nothing calls it
findings.description: signIn(), the `stage` state, `busy`, `label` and `evm = detectEvmWallet()` are all defined in Login but no JSX references signIn or label, and `stage` is only ever 'idle' so `busy` is permanently false (the 'Remember me' checkbox's disabled={!!busy} can never fire). findings.fix: Delete signIn/stage/busy/label/evm from Login (and the now-unused connectRobinhoodChain/detectEvmWallet/ROBINHOOD_CHAIN imports), or re-expose a wallet button if that path is meant to exist.

findings.title: No eol normalization: autocrlf=true causes LF->CRLF warnings and whole-file diffs
findings.description: .gitattributes only declares the mp4 LFS filter; there is no `* text=auto` rule. With core.autocrlf=true on this machine, git already warns that docs/CARDS.txt and src/cards.test.ts will be rewritten to CRLF, which produces whole-file diffs for anyone on macOS/Linux or in CI and makes `git blame` useless on touched files.

warning: in the working copy of 'src/cards.test.ts', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it

*.mp4 filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text
$ git config core.autocrlf
true
findings.fix: Add `* text=auto eol=lf` (plus binary markers for png/webp/woff2/glb/mp3) to .gitattributes and run `git add --renormalize .` once.

findings.title: The card face is rendered seven different ways with copy-pasted cost-pip logic
findings.description: CardFace and MiniCard (Board), HubCardTile and LibraryRow (App), CardPreview/TemplatedPreview (CardPreview.tsx), Tutorial.MiniCard, Boosters.RevealCard and the dead DeckBuilderCard each re-derive the same things: total cost via `Object.values(def.cost).reduce`, the `['any', ...COLORS]` pip row with the `#c8c8d0/#1a1a1a` grey, P/T minus damage, fullCard vs template branching. They already disagree: Board's CardFace hides rules text on compact, HubCardTile shows cost as a number not pips, Tutorial.MiniCard replaces '~' with the card name while the others print '~' literally. A card-text or cost-format change must be made in seven places.

findings.description: Git tracks docs/CARDS.txt but the working tree contains docs/cards.txt (241 KB, regenerated 2026-10-29). With core.ignorecase=true on Windows git treats them as the same file, so the regeneration shows up as a 2,842-line modification to CARDS.txt and will be committed under the upper-case name, while a Linux checkout (Vercel, CI, collaborators) sees only CARDS.txt and any tooling expecting cards.txt fails. findings.title: `anchor` npm dependency is the unrelated Sails.js validator, not @coral-xyz/anchor
findings.description: package.json still declares "anchor": "^1.4.2". findings.title: Anchor oracle settle path has no draw/cancel handling and is dead code
findings.description: settleWagerMatch returns without acting on a draw ('no settle path yet'), which would leave both stakes locked in the on-chain match forever, and oracleCancel is a stub. server.ts no longer imports this module (the comment at line 566 says the Anchor path was removed), so it is unreachable money code that still reads SOLANA_ORACLE_KEYPAIR at import time if called.
findings.fix: Delete src/server-wager.ts and src/wager-program.ts's settle helpers, or finish the draw/expire path before anything imports it again.

findings.title: Foundry suite covers only WagerEscrow happy paths; libs not installed and no CI runs forge
findings.description: The only test file exercises settle, draw, two reverts, three reclaim cases and one rake fuzz. Untested: cancelMatch, every admin setter (setRake/setOperator/setTimeouts), settle with a non-participant winner, deposit by a non-player, double settle, settle after reclaim, claim with zero credits, fee-on-transfer tokens, a global solvency invariant (sum(credits) <= balance), and CardPack/MasterToken entirely (the two contracts holding real ETH and controlling supply). contracts/lib does not exist in the checkout (remappings point at lib/forge-std and lib/openzeppelin-contracts) and no workflow invokes forge, so even these tests are not run anywhere automatically. Audit L-7, unchanged.
findings.fix: Add CardPack.t.sol (price, overpay, receiver-revert re-roll, withdraw) and MasterToken.t.sol, add the missing WagerEscrow negative/admin tests plus an invariant test for solvency, vendor or submodule the libs, and add a GitHub Actions job that runs forge test.

findings.title: Legacy boot has no graceful shutdown or unhandledRejection handler
findings.description: The server starts with an IIFE and never registers SIGTERM/SIGINT or unhandledRejection handlers. Background timers (matchmaker, telemetry/replay flushers, custodial RPC retries) keep running during a Render deploy until the process is killed, and any stray rejection in those timers crashes the process with Node's default behaviour mid-settlement.
findings.fix: Handle SIGTERM by stopping timers, closing the HTTP server and draining the pool (new-backend/packages/shared/src/service.ts shows the pattern).

findings.description: A symbol-usage scan of App.tsx finds these defined-but-never-referenced components: RulesPage (716-1049) and its exclusive helpers RuleSection, renderSectionBody, LifeOrb, CardTypesGrid, GasFlowViz, FlowNode, FlowArrow, TurnTimeline, ExampleTurn, RULES_NAV, RULES_SEARCH_INDEX, SECTION_SUMMARY (~730 lines); MenuRow, ProfileTopBar, ProfileSkeleton, ProfileHero, PlayerStats, AchievementGrid, EmptyState, Mini, DeckBuilderCard, FilterChip, ColorChooser, Section, Banner, WAGERS_AVAILABLE, inputStyle, cardStyle, primaryBtn, disabledBtn, tinyBtn. findings.title: App.tsx is a 8,479-line god module holding 13 distinct screens plus the router
findings.description: App.tsx contains every screen, its design tokens, its data hooks and the root router in one file, so any change re-typechecks and re-bundles everything and reviewers cannot own a screen. Distinct units and their line ranges: Login + WalletLinkPrompt (223-563); BgMusic/MenuMusic/BattleMusic (572-656); RulesPage subsystem (658-1446, DEAD, see frontend-07); RulebookPage + RB_* data + RuleSearch (1448-2017); Landing hub: MENU tokens, Landing, PlayerHUD, MatchmakingPanel, HubRankedDeckNote, ActivityPanel, NavDock, TokenAnnouncement (2021-2820); Profile hub: HUB tokens, ProfilePage, HubTopNav, IdentityBar, OverviewTab, CollectionTab, AchievementsTab, chips, HubCardTile (2822-3502); Deck builder: DeckWorkspace, LibraryRow, CurrentDeckPanel, SavedDeckLibrary (3505-4136); legacy profile widgets + ProfileEditModal (4138-4619, mostly dead); PublicProfile + dead DeckBuilderCard/FilterChip (4622-4920); Lobby and its 15 panels (4922-6355); MatchSeat waiting room + MatchLoadingScreen + deep-link helpers (6358-6752); PrintAllCards, SoloSetupModal, InstallPrompt (6759-7066); App root + SessionBootstrap (7074-7560); Ranked: useRankedQueue, RankedQueueControl, RankedPage and panels (7562-8323); legacy Screen/Section/Banner/WagerControls/ColorChooser (8326-8479). The root itself routes with a 40-line nested ternary and passes screen state through sessionStorage side channels (editProfile at 7471 sets 'ocva.openProfileEdit' for ProfilePage to read at 2855).

findings.title: Dead modules: boosters-api.ts, server-wager.ts, wager-program.ts (client side)
findings.description: `src/boosters-api.ts` is imported by nothing (only mentioned in a comment in pack-evm.ts). `src/server-wager.ts` is imported by nothing; `src/wager-program.ts` is reached only from `server-custodial.ts` and `solana/scripts/initialize.ts`, and ends with the `void Keypair;` hack to silence an unused import. All of them are inside `tsconfig include: ["src"]`, so they are type-checked on every `npm run build` and carry a full Solana wager program ABI that the product no longer uses (wagers are EVM, server-side, per `src/api/wager.ts`). This is confusing for anyone auditing "where does money move".
findings.fix: Delete `boosters-api.ts` and `server-wager.ts`; move `wager-program.ts` under `solana/` next to its only consumer, or delete it with `server-custodial.ts` if the legacy Koa server is retired.
